item.stdout:
Check 1 — Licensure
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 6:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive professional medical licenses will be verified."
"Licenses will be verified before expiration."
and, on what a licence has to be:
"Every licensed practitioner who provides patient care in federal facilities must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States."
Larkhollow rule — the practice state. The manual's sentence above is a federal facility's rule: it accepts a licence from any State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or a territory, and Section 15 says so again, answering the question "Where is it documented that a practitioner does not need to be licensed in the state where they provide services in a federal facility?" with
"Federal law at 25 U.S.C. § 1621t states that licensed health professionals employed by a tribal health program are exempt if licensed in any state, from the licensure requirements of the state where services under an ISDEAA agreement are performed."
We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us. Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.
Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
Larkhollow rule — where the five years are measured from. The manual states the window and not its anchor. Ours is the date the application was first received: an entry is inside the window when any part of it falls in the five years counted back from the date the application was first received. A later revision does not move the anchor.
Element 4 defines a gap and says what is owed:
"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"
"Verification of time gaps is not required, but an explanation is."
Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.

Check 1 — Licensure
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 6:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive professional medical licenses will be verified."
"Licenses will be verified before expiration."
and, on what a licence has to be:
"Every licensed practitioner who provides patient care in federal facilities must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States."
Larkhollow rule — the practice state. The manual's sentence above is a federal facility's rule: it accepts a licence from any State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or a territory, and Section 15 says so again, answering the question "Where is it documented that a practitioner does not need to be licensed in the state where they provide services in a federal facility?" with
"Federal law at 25 U.S.C. § 1621t states that licensed health professionals employed by a tribal health program are exempt if licensed in any state, from the licensure requirements of the state where services under an ISDEAA agreement are performed."
We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us. Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.
Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
Larkhollow rule — where the five years are measured from. The manual states the window and not its anchor. Ours is the date the application was first received: an entry is inside the window when any part of it falls in the five years counted back from the date the application was first received. A later revision does not move the anchor.
Element 4 defines a gap and says what is owed:
"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"
"Verification of time gaps is not required, but an explanation is."
Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.

Check 1 — Licensure
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 6:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive professional medical licenses will be verified."
"Licenses will be verified before expiration."
and, on what a licence has to be:
"Every licensed practitioner who provides patient care in federal facilities must possess a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a State, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, or a territory of the United States."
Larkhollow rule — the practice state. The manual's sentence above is a federal facility's rule: it accepts a licence from any State, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico or a territory, and Section 15 says so again, answering the question "Where is it documented that a practitioner does not need to be licensed in the state where they provide services in a federal facility?" with
"Federal law at 25 U.S.C. § 1621t states that licensed health professionals employed by a tribal health program are exempt if licensed in any state, from the licensure requirements of the state where services under an ISDEAA agreement are performed."
We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us. Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.
Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
Larkhollow rule — where the five years are measured from. The manual states the window and not its anchor. Ours is the date the application was first received: an entry is inside the window when any part of it falls in the five years counted back from the date the application was first received. A later revision does not move the anchor.
Element 4 defines a gap and says what is owed:
"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"
"Verification of time gaps is not required, but an explanation is."
Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
Larkhollow rule — what the office does with a gap. We record the gap and we record the applicant's written explanation beside it. An explanation names the period it covers, and it covers a gap only when that named period runs from at or before the gap's first day to at or after the gap's last day. A gap with a written explanation covering it is marked explained. A gap with no written explanation is unexplained, and the application is returned as incomplete under the manual's sentence quoted in section 1. The office marks a gap explained on the presence of a written explanation and on nothing else. We do not read the explanation and decide whether it is good enough. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8:
"current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the MSP."
Larkhollow rule — the long gap. Any gap of 180 days or more is routed to the Clinical Director for a recorded disposition, whether or not it carries an explanation. The Clinical Director decides; the office supplies the gap, the explanation and the verified dates.
Check 3 — Professional education and post-graduate training
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"A qualifying degree is the degree required for the applicant's position and privileges."
"such as internship, residency, fellowship, or other organized professional training will be verified."
So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
Check 4 — Professional peer references
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
Check 6 — The committee decision
Covered in sections 8 and 9.
4. High-risk findings
The manual, Section 7:
"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
Both halves apply here. A Yes on the disclosure page is a high-risk finding. So is a No that the evidence contradicts — a board record showing an action against a licence beside a No to the question about licence restrictions is the second half, and the applicant is contacted to confirm the response.
Larkhollow rule — where a high-risk finding goes. The Clinical Director is alerted, and the file is presented to the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff and to the Governing Body with the evidence. The manual's Section 7 also routes such a file to an Agency Clinical Credentials Committee for an endorsement determination; that body is a federal agency committee and there is no equivalent at Larkhollow. That route is out of scope for us. No third body exists here.
5. Privilege requests
Every application names the privilege groups it requests, from the current published criteria. The manual, Section 5, makes it a completeness condition:
"a request for specific privileges is received;"
An applicant may amend the requested set by submitting a revision.
6. Reserved judgments
Five judgments are not the office's and never become the office's, no matter how obvious the answer looks from the file.

We are not a federal facility and that exemption does not reach us. Larkhollow's bylaws require a practitioner to hold one current, active, full and unrestricted licence issued by the State of Washington, which is our practice state. Every other licence the applicant holds, active or inactive, in any state, is still verified under the manual's sentence above — we verify them all; only one of them satisfies the bylaw.

The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.

A later revision does not move the anchor.

"A time gap is 30 or more days when the LP is not in school or training, in the military, teaching, working,"

Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.

+    "Vice-Chair, Governing Body": ("Mr. Desmond Ihejirika", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)),
+    "Chair, Executive Committee of the Medical Staff": ("Dr. Peter Vandermolen, MD", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2027, 12, 31)),
+    "Chair, Credentials Committee": ("Dr. Anneke Thorvald, MD", date(2025, 7, 1), date(2027, 6, 30)),
+}
+_BODY_OUTCOMES = {
+    "Credentials Committee": {"recommended", "not recommended", "deferred-pending-information"},
+    "Executive Committee of the Medical Staff": {"recommended", "not recommended", "deferred-pending-information"},
+    "Governing Body": {"approved", "approved-with-conditions", "deferred-pending-information", "denied"},
+}
+
+
+def _fields(markdown: str) -> dict[str, str]:
+    return {k.strip().casefold(): v.strip() for k, v in re.findall(r"^\*\*([^*]+):\*\*\s*(.*?)\s*$", markdown, re.M)}
+
+
+def _document_ref(batch: dict[str, Any], doc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    return {"batch_id": batch.get("batch_id"), "document_path": doc.get("path"), "sha256": doc.get("sha256")}
+
+
+def _app_revision_exists(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, revision: str, on: date) -> bool:
+    return any(r.get("filename") == "applications.csv"
+               and str(r.get("values", {}).get("application_id")) == app_id
+               and str(r.get("values", {}).get("revision")) == revision
+               and (_parse_date(b.get("export_date")) or date.min) <= on
+               for b, r in _row_records(ledger, on))
+
+
+def _dispositions(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, revision: str, as_of: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    found = []
+    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
+        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
+            continue
+        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
+            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
+            if "/dispositions/" not in f"/{path}" or not content:
+                continue
+            f = _fields(content)
+            aid = f.get("application", "")
+            rev = f.get("revision", revision)
+            if aid == app_id and str(rev) == str(revision):
+                date_match = _parse_date(f.get("date"))
+                if date_match and date_match <= as_of:
+                    found.append({"fields": f, "content": content, "ref": _document_ref(batch, doc), "date": date_match})
+    return found
+
+
+def assess_packet_readiness(ledger: dict[str, Any], application_id: str, revision: int | str, as_of: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Assess six-element readiness as of a date, with authorized dispositions."""
+    day = _parse_date(as_of)
+    if day is None:
+        raise ValueError("as_of must be an ISO calendar date")
+    ev = evaluate_application(ledger, application_id, revision, as_of)
+    dispositions = _dispositions(ledger, application_id, str(revision), day)
+    cleared: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    blockers: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
+    for name, detail in ev["element_details"].items():
+        state = detail["state"]
+        obs = detail.get("observations", [])
+        for finding in obs:
+            code = finding.get("code", "")
+            if code in {"licensure_finding", "gap_disposition_pending", "threshold_eligibility_question", "high_risk_finding"}:
+                matching = [d for d in dispositions if "Clinical Director" in d["content"] and
+                            (code != "gap_disposition_pending" or "gap" in d["content"].casefold()) and
+                            (code != "licensure_finding" or "licens" in d["content"].casefold())]
+                if matching:
+                    cleared.append({"element": name, "finding_code": code, "disposition": matching[-1]["ref"], "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+                    continue
+                blockers.append({"element": name, "code": code, "message": finding.get("message", "Required disposition is missing."), "evidence": finding.get("evidence", detail.get("evidence", [])), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+            elif state != "resolved":
+                blockers.append({"element": name, "code": code or state, "message": finding.get("message", f"Element state is {state}."), "evidence": finding.get("evidence", detail.get("evidence", [])), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+        # No observations for a non-resolved state still constitutes blocking work.
+        if state != "resolved" and not obs:
+            blockers.append({"element": name, "code": state, "message": f"Element state is {state}.", "evidence": detail.get("evidence", []), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+    # High-risk disclosure evidence is outside the six element states.
+    for batch, record in _row_records(ledger, day):
+        v = record.get("values", {})
+        if record.get("filename") == "application-disclosures.csv" and v.get("application_id") == application_id and str(v.get("revision")) == str(revision) and str(v.get("answer", "")).casefold() == "yes":
+            refs = [_source_ref(batch, record)]
+            matching = [d for d in dispositions if "Clinical Director" in d["content"] and "high-risk" in d["content"].casefold()]
+            if not matching:
+                blockers.append({"element": "high-risk", "code": "high_risk_disposition_pending", "message": "High-risk disclosure awaits a Clinical Director disposition.", "evidence": refs, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+            else:
+                cleared.append({"element": "high-risk", "finding_code": "high_risk_finding", "disposition": matching[-1]["ref"], "evidence": refs, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
+    return {"application_id": application_id, "revision": int(revision), "as_of": as_of,
+            "presentable": not blockers, "elements": ev["elements"], "blockers": blockers,
+            "cleared_holds": cleared, "evaluation": ev, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"],
+            "limitations": LIMITATIONS}
+
+
+def _parse_decisions(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
+    out = []
+    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
+        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
+            continue
+        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
+            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
+            if "/decisions/" not in f"/{path}" or not content:
+                continue
+            f = _fields(content)
+            if not f.get("decision id"):
+                continue
+            f["__ref"] = _document_ref(batch, doc)
+            f["__content"] = content
+            out.append(f)
+    return out
+
+
+def _admit_decision(ledger: dict[str, Any], d: dict[str, Any], target_app: str, target_rev: str, readiness_cache: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
+    decision_date = _parse_date(d.get("decision date"))
+    app_id, rev, body = d.get("application", ""), d.get("revision", ""), d.get("body", "")
+    outcome = d.get("outcome", "").casefold()
+    role, signatory = d.get("role", ""), d.get("signatory", "")
+    if body not in _BODY_OUTCOMES or outcome not in _BODY_OUTCOMES.get(body, set()): return False, "body-or-outcome-not-authorized"
+    if decision_date is None: return False, "invalid-decision-date"
+    if body == "Governing Body":
+        authorized = signatory == "Ms. Corinne Batiste" and role == "Chair, Governing Body"
+        authorized |= (signatory == "Mr. Desmond Ihejirika" and role == "Vice-Chair, Governing Body" and date(2026,1,5) <= decision_date <= date(2026,12,31))
+    else:
+        expected = _ROLES.get(role)
+        authorized = bool(expected and expected[0] == signatory and expected[1] <= decision_date <= expected[2] and
+                          ((body == "Executive Committee of the Medical Staff" and role == "Chair, Executive Committee of the Medical Staff") or (body == "Credentials Committee" and role == "Chair, Credentials Committee")))
+    if not authorized: return False, "signatory-not-authorized-on-decision-date"
+    if not app_id or not rev or not _app_revision_exists(ledger, app_id, rev, decision_date): return False, "application-revision-not-on-file"
+    if app_id != target_app: return False, "decision-names-different-application"
+    # The record must have a presentable packet before its decision date.
+    prior_day = decision_date - timedelta(days=1)
+    key = (app_id, str(rev), prior_day.isoformat())
+    if key not in readiness_cache: readiness_cache[key] = assess_packet_readiness(ledger, app_id, rev, prior_day.isoformat())
+    if not readiness_cache[key]["presentable"]: return False, "packet-not-presentable-before-decision-date"
+    if outcome not in {"approved", "approved-with-conditions", "deferred-pending-information", "denied", "recommended", "not recommended"}: return False, "invalid-outcome"
+    reason_required = outcome in {"approved-with-conditions", "deferred-pending-information", "denied", "not recommended"}
+    if reason_required and not d.get("reason"): return False, "required-reason-missing"
+    if outcome == "deferred-pending-information" and not d.get("reason"): return False, "deferral-information-not-named"
+    if body == "Governing Body" and outcome in {"approved", "approved-with-conditions", "denied", "deferred-pending-information"}:
+        prior = [x for x in _parse_decisions(ledger, decision_date) if x.get("application") == app_id and x.get("revision") == rev and x.get("body") == "Governing Body" and (_parse_date(x.get("decision date")) or date.max) < decision_date]
+        if prior and d.get("supersedes") != prior[-1].get("decision id"): return False, "second-governing-body-decision-must-supersede-earlier"
+    return True, None
+
+
+def process_recorded_decisions(ledger: dict[str, Any], application_id: str, revision: int | str, as_of: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Return the schema-compatible decision/activation fragment and audit detail."""
+    day = _parse_date(as_of)
+    if day is None: raise ValueError("as_of must be an ISO calendar date")
+    rev = str(revision)
+    docs = [d for d in _parse_decisions(ledger, day) if d.get("application") == application_id]
+    cache: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    records, details = [], []
+    admitted = []
+    for d in docs:
+        ok, reason = _admit_decision(ledger, d, application_id, rev, cache)
+        records.append({"decision_id": d["decision id"], "admitted": ok, "reason": None if ok else reason})
+        details.append({"decision_id": d["decision id"], "application_id": d.get("application"), "revision": d.get("revision"), "body": d.get("body"), "signatory": d.get("signatory"), "role": d.get("role"), "decision_date": d.get("decision date"), "outcome": d.get("outcome"), "reason": d.get("reason") or None, "supersedes": d.get("supersedes") or None, "source": d["__ref"], "admitted": ok, "admission_reason": reason, "rule_refs": POLICY["decisions"]})
+        if ok and str(d.get("revision")) == rev: admitted.append(d)
+    governing = [d for d in admitted if d.get("body") == "Governing Body"]
+    governing.sort(key=lambda d: (_parse_date(d.get("decision date")) or date.min, d["decision id"]))
+    final = governing[-1] if governing else None
+    approval_id = None
+    activation = None
+    conditions = []
+    status = "decision-inadmissible" if any(not r["admitted"] for r in records) else "packet-presentable"
+    readiness = assess_packet_readiness(ledger, application_id, revision, as_of)
+    if not readiness["presentable"]: status = "in-verification"
+    if final:
+        out = final.get("outcome", "").casefold()
+        if out == "deferred-pending-information": status = "deferred"
+        elif out == "denied": status = "denied"
+        elif out in {"approved", "approved-with-conditions"}:
+            approval_id = final["decision id"]
+            effective = _parse_date(final.get("effective date")) or _parse_date(final.get("decision date"))
+            cycle_end = effective.replace(year=effective.year + 1) - timedelta(days=1) if effective.month != 2 or effective.day != 29 else date(effective.year + 1, 2, 28)
+            privileges = sorted({p.strip() for p in final.get("privileges", "").split(";") if p.strip()})
+            active = effective <= day and day <= cycle_end and bool(privileges)
+            activation = {"active_at_export": active, "effective_date": effective.isoformat(), "cycle_end": cycle_end.isoformat(), "privileges": privileges}
+            if not active: status = "approved-not-yet-effective" if day < effective else "in-verification"
+            elif out == "approved-with-conditions": status = "active-with-conditions"
+            else: status = "active"
+            if out == "approved-with-conditions":
+                # Conditions are explicitly supplied as semicolon-delimited `condition due YYYY-MM-DD` items in Reason.
+                for item in (final.get("reason") or "").split(";"):
+                    m = re.match(r"\s*(.*?)\s+due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$", item, re.I)
+                    if m and _parse_date(m.group(2)):
+                        conditions.append({"condition": m.group(1).strip(), "due": m.group(2)})
+    return {"application_id": application_id, "revision": int(revision), "as_of": as_of,
+            "schema_compatible": {"status": status, "elements": readiness["elements"], "packet_presentable": readiness["presentable"], "decisions": records, "approval_decision_id": approval_id, "activation": activation, "monitored_conditions": conditions, "action_queue": []},
+            "readiness": readiness, "decision_details": details, "rule_refs": {**POLICY}, "limitations": LIMITATIONS}
*** End Patch";

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Ingest one closed Project E batch into an append-only evidence ledger."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent))

from credentialing.ingestion import empty_ledger, ingest_batch, load_ledger


def save_ledger(path: Path, ledger: dict) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    descriptor, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp", dir=path.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as output:
            json.dump(ledger, output, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
            output.write("\n")
            output.flush()
            os.fsync(output.fileno())
        os.replace(temporary_name, path)
    except BaseException:
        try:
            os.unlink(temporary_name)
        except OSError:
            pass
        raise


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Ingest a batch export without applying credentialing decisions.")
    parser.add_argument("batch_dir", type=Path, help="directory containing one batch README, CSVs, and indexed documents")
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, help="existing evidence ledger to merge into")
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, help="ledger output path (defaults to --ledger, or deliverables/evidence-ledger.json)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        current = load_ledger(args.ledger) if args.ledger else empty_ledger()
        result = ingest_batch(args.batch_dir, current)
        output_path = args.output or args.ledger or Path("deliverables/evidence-ledger.json")
        if result.changed:
            save_ledger(output_path, result.ledger)
        elif args.ledger is None and result.batch_id is None:
            # A new run with an unreadable README has nothing safe to serialize.
            pass
    except (OSError, ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        print(f"Ingestion failed: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    if result.changed:
        print(f"Ingested {result.batch_id} into {output_path}")
    else:
        print(f"No ledger changes for {result.batch_id or args.batch_dir}")
    for issue in result.issues:
        location = issue.filename or "batch"
        if issue.row_number is not None:
            location += f":{issue.row_number}"
        print(f"{issue.code} [{location}]: {issue.message}", file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if result.issues else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

item.stdout:
office/peer-reference-form.txt:1:Professional peer reference — blank request and return form
office/peer-reference-form.txt-2-Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Form version LARK-REF-2026.1.
office/peer-reference-form.txt-3-The office sends this form directly to the referee the applicant named, and the referee returns it directly to the office. A form that reaches us through the applicant cannot be used.
--
office/peer-reference-form.txt-22-	What to enter
office/peer-reference-form.txt-23-	Are you a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant?
office/peer-reference-form.txt:24:	Tick Yes or No. This box is never left blank
office/peer-reference-form.txt-25-	Relationship
office/peer-reference-form.txt-26-	How you worked with the applicant, in your own words
--
office/peer-reference-form.txt-28-	The clinical discipline you practise, chosen from the same list the applicant chose from: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Hospital Medicine, Cardiovascular Disease, Emergency Medicine, General Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynecology, Pediatrics, Anesthesiology, Diagnostic Radiology, Psychiatry, Orthopaedic Surgery — or your own discipline if it is not on that list
office/peer-reference-form.txt-29-	Dates you worked directly together
office/peer-reference-form.txt:30:	First and last date. Leave the last date blank only if you still work together
office/peer-reference-form.txt-31-	Recommendation
office/peer-reference-form.txt-32-	Recommend without reservation, Recommend, Recommend with reservations, or Do not recommend
--
office/peer-reference-form.txt-35-	Signature and signature date
office/peer-reference-form.txt-36-	The date you sign. This is the date we measure currency from — not the date we receive the form
office/peer-reference-form.txt:37:	Who may give a peer reference
office/peer-reference-form.txt-38-Three conditions, each independent, all three required:
office/peer-reference-form.txt-39-1. you have worked directly with the applicant within the two years ending on the day you sign this form;
office/peer-reference-form.txt-40-2. you practise in the same clinical discipline as the applicant;
office/peer-reference-form.txt-41-3. you are not a relative, spouse or partner of the applicant.
office/peer-reference-form.txt:42:If any one of the three does not hold, say so on the form and return it anyway. We will record your reply, and we will not count it towards the two references the appointment needs. That is not a judgment about you or about the applicant; it is the rule we apply to every file the same way.
office/peer-reference-form.txt-43-Currency
office/peer-reference-form.txt:44:A reference is current if the signature date is within two years of the date the file is presented to the Governing Body. A reference signed a long time before the file is presented stops being current, and we ask again.
office/peer-reference-form.txt-45-________________
office/peer-reference-form.txt-46-Part 3 — completed by the Medical Staff Office on return
--
office/privilege-criteria.txt-2-Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Criteria version LARK-PRIV-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Set by the Clinical Director with the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff. Published and applied by the Medical Staff Office. The office applies these criteria; the office does not write them and does not extend them for an individual applicant.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-3-Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. A file decided under one version is not re-read under another; a new version re-opens the mapping for files not yet decided.
office/privilege-criteria.txt:4:The manual we adopted says what criteria must cover, in Section 9: "At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience." The three columns below are those three.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-5-The twelve privilege groups
office/privilege-criteria.txt:6:Every group requires a Doctor of Medicine or Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine degree from an accredited school, so the education level is not repeated in each row.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-7-Code
office/privilege-criteria.txt-8-	Privilege group
--
office/privilege-criteria.txt-13-	Family Medicine — outpatient and inpatient care of patients of any age
office/privilege-criteria.txt-14-	American Board of Family Medicine (ABFM), Family Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Family Physicians (AOBFP), Family Practice
office/privilege-criteria.txt:15:	Completion of an accredited family medicine residency, 36 months

office/privilege-criteria.txt-23-	Hospital Medicine — adult inpatient care, admission and attending
office/privilege-criteria.txt-24-	American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Internal Medicine; American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM), Internal Medicine with Focused Practice in Hospital Medicine; American Board of Family Medicine (ABFM), Family Medicine; American Osteopathic Board of Internal Medicine (AOBIM), Internal Medicine
office/privilege-criteria.txt:25:	Completion of an accredited internal medicine residency or an accredited family medicine residency, 36 months

command:
python3 - <<'PY'
import json
from credentialing.readiness import assess_packet_readiness,_historical_evidence_view
from credentialing.ingestion import load_ledger
from datetime import date
l=load_ledger('/tmp/project-e-stage4-batch1-ledger.json')
for aid,day in [('APP-2026-001','2026-03-09'),('APP-2026-003','2026-03-11'),('APP-2026-007','2026-03-09'),('APP-2026-013','2026-03-11'),('APP-2026-014','2026-03-09'),('APP-2026-036','2026-03-09')]:
 r=assess_packet_readiness(_historical_evidence_view(l,date.fromisoformat(day)),aid,1,day)
 print(aid,day, {k:v['state'] for k,v in r['evaluation']['element_details'].items()})
 for b in r['blockers']:
  print(' ',b['element'],b['code'],b['message'])
PY

﻿Accepted sources by element — who may attest
Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office Table version LARK-ATT-2026.1, in force from 2026-01-01. Maintained by the Medical Services Professional.
The manual we adopted leaves its source lists open. Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends "etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications", and element 5 ends "or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications".
Larkhollow rule. An open list cannot be applied the same way twice, so ours is closed. This table is the whole list. A reply from a source on it is admissible. A reply from any source not on it is inadmissible and is raised to the Medical Services Professional — it is not quietly accepted, and it is not quietly treated as a secondary source.
Two rules cut across every row, both the manual's, both from Section 6, Subsection 1:
"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
So the applicant is never an accepted source for any element, on any row below, however genuine the document they carry. The reply is filed as received and the request stays open.
Education and training
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The degree-granting school's registrar's office or dean's office. The sponsoring institution's graduate medical education office or programme director, for a residency or fellowship
	Designated equivalent source
	Educational Commission for Foreign Medical Graduates (ECFMG). Federation Credentials Verification Service of the Federation of State Medical Boards (FCVS). American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. National Student Clearinghouse
	Secondary source — only on impossibility
	The applicant's most recent affiliation's medical staff office, stating how it obtained its own verification, when the school or programme has closed and no designated equivalent source holds the record. The reason is written into the file
	Not accepted
	The applicant. An alumni association. A departmental colleague writing in a personal capacity. A recruiter, staffing agency or locum tenens agency. A photocopied or scanned certificate from any hand
	Licensure
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The issuing state licensing board, through its own online verification service or a written reply from the board
	Designated equivalent source
	Federation of State Medical Boards Physician Data Center
	Secondary source
	None. A state licensing board does not close
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A prior employer's copy of a licence. An aggregator or directory not named above
	Board certification
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The issuing certifying board, through its own verification service or a written reply
	Designated equivalent source
	American Board of Medical Specialties (ABMS) certification verification. CertiFACTS. American Medical Association Physician Profile. American Osteopathic Association Physician Profile. American Board of Physician Specialties (ABPS). American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC). National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA)
	Secondary source
	None
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A certificate image. A specialty society membership roster
	Affiliations and employment
Class
	Accepted sources
	Primary source
	The affiliated hospital's medical staff office. The employer's human resources department or the practice's authorized administrator
	Designated equivalent source
	A credentials verification organization retained by that affiliation or employer, where the reply names the organization and the affiliation it acted for
	Secondary source — only on impossibility
	Where the employer has dissolved and no successor holds the records, a written account from the applicant's most recent surviving affiliation of what that affiliation verified, with the reason written into the file
	Not accepted
	The applicant. A supervisor writing from a personal address without the employer's authority. A professional networking profile. A letter of recommendation offered in place of a dates-and-position verification
	What to do with a reply that is not on this table
1. Record it as received, with who sent it and how it arrived. Nothing is discarded.
2. Mark the entry still outstanding. An inadmissible reply does not resolve anything.
3. Keep requesting from a source that is on the table, and keep logging each attempt.
4. Raise it to the Medical Services Professional, who decides whether the case is one of the impossibility routes above.
Non-response is not impossibility. A source that exists and does not answer is a non-responsive source: it stays outstanding, the attempts keep being logged, and the manual's red flag applies. Only a source that no longer exists opens the secondary route.

## Batch 1 audit

I ingested Batch 1 into a temporary ledger at `/tmp/project-e-stage4-batch1-ledger.json`. Ingestion reported **0 integrity issues**. The batch contains **40 applications and 41 application revisions**.
