office/procedure-extract.txt:5:Larkhollow is a community hospital. It is not a federal facility. We adopted the verification standard work published by the Indian Health Service in its Medical Staff Credentialing and Privileging Standard Operating Procedure Manual, Version 8.0, September 2025, as our own written procedure, because it is a complete, current and publicly stated account of how the work is done.
office/procedure-extract.txt:10:The office also runs identity verification, controlled-substance registrations, the National Practitioner Data Bank query, sanctions and exclusion lookups, life support certificates, continuing education, immunization records, liability coverage and malpractice history. Those are handled outside this procedure and are not part of the work described here.
office/procedure-extract.txt:17:"a signed IHS Conditions of Application & Release is received (required to be able to conduct any verifications);"
office/procedure-extract.txt:19:Larkhollow rule. Our equivalent of that release is the Larkhollow Authorization and Release, printed inside the application. It is our own form; the manual's is a federal instrument and we do not use it. The rule it carries is the manual's and we keep it: until a signed release is on file we send no verification request of any kind. A file with no signed release cannot advance, no matter how much else is present.
office/procedure-extract.txt:27:7. at least two peer referees are named, with a working address for each;
office/procedure-extract.txt:28:8. every declared affiliation and employer carries a verification contact;
office/procedure-extract.txt:36:Before and during verification we read the curriculum vitae against the application, and then both against whatever the sources return. The manual, Section 6, Subsection 2:
office/procedure-extract.txt:37:"The MSP will compare the CV/resume with the application and completed verifications and correct or resolve any discrepancies."
office/procedure-extract.txt:38:"There must be a follow-up of any verification discrepancies found during the application and"
office/procedure-extract.txt:45:Larkhollow rule — a revision is reconciled, not assumed. When a revision arrives, the reconciliation above runs again on what the revision says, against the curriculum vitae and against every verification already completed on the entries it touches. Dates are not the only thing a revision can move: the organization, the role, the supervisor and the verification contact all belong to the entry, and a change to any of them is a change to the entry. Section 11 says what re-opens when it does. The monitoring duty in section 11 runs alongside it and does not pause while a file waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt:47:Six elements are verified in this procedure: licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. The manual numbers seventeen essential credentialing elements in Section 6, Subsection 4. Of the other eleven, nine are handled by the office outside this procedure, as stated above; current competency is the clinical leadership's, not the office's; and the manual's conditions-and-release form is replaced by our own Authorization and Release, which is part of intake in this procedure.
office/procedure-extract.txt:48:What counts as a verification at all
office/procedure-extract.txt:49:The manual, Section 1, defines primary source verification as
office/procedure-extract.txt:52:"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
office/procedure-extract.txt:53:"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
office/procedure-extract.txt:54:A reply that reached us through the applicant is not a verification, however genuine the document looks, however clear the letterhead, however real the registrar's signature. It goes in the file as received and the request stays open.
office/procedure-extract.txt:56:"etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications"
office/procedure-extract.txt:58:"or other nationally recognized certifying body, as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for board certification verifications"
office/procedure-extract.txt:61:"If completing primary or DES verifications is impossible, such as when an educational institution or residency program has closed, secondary source verifications may be used."
office/procedure-extract.txt:62:"When a primary or designated equivalent source cannot be obtained, the applicant's recent affiliations should be contacted to discover how they obtained the verification."
office/procedure-extract.txt:67:"Each attempt, including whom it was attempted to verify with, the date of request, verification methods, and any additional comments, is documented in the Notes section of the entry."
office/procedure-extract.txt:70:"If the affiliation is unwilling to complete the verification or is non-responsive after 3 attempts, this should be noted as a red flag."
office/procedure-extract.txt:85:"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
office/procedure-extract.txt:86:The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
office/procedure-extract.txt:96:Larkhollow rule — how the gap list is computed. The clock starts on the day after the applicant finished professional school. Every declared entry of any type covers every day from its start date to its end date inclusive; an entry with no end date runs to the export date. Overlapping entries, part-time appointments and training years are covering entries: an overlap covers, it does not create a gap. A gap is a run of 30 or more consecutive days that no entry covers. The list is recomputed from scratch whenever a revision or a verification changes a date; it is not patched.
office/procedure-extract.txt:104:So: the qualifying degree, and every post-graduate training entry. The accepted sources are in attester-table.md. The admissibility rules are the ones in "What counts as a verification at all" above — the applicant may not carry the reply, and a source not on the table is raised.
office/procedure-extract.txt:107:Check 4 — Professional peer references
office/procedure-extract.txt:109:"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
office/procedure-extract.txt:110:"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
office/procedure-extract.txt:115:* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
office/procedure-extract.txt:119:"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
office/procedure-extract.txt:120:The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt:121:Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
office/procedure-extract.txt:122:Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
office/procedure-extract.txt:123:Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt:124:Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt:133:and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
office/procedure-extract.txt:134:"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
office/procedure-extract.txt:135:Larkholl…628 tokens truncated…ow, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
office/procedure-extract.txt:181:For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
office/procedure-extract.txt:183:Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:194:Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible. All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
office/procedure-extract.txt:196:2. the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
office/procedure-extract.txt:197:3. the decision names the same applicant and the same application revision as the presentable packet;
office/procedure-extract.txt:198:4. a presentable packet existed for that revision before the decision date;
office/procedure-extract.txt:200:A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:201:Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision. It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
office/procedure-extract.txt:202:Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision. A second decision for the same application revision is admissible only when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
office/procedure-extract.txt:203:Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision. recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
office/procedure-extract.txt:212:Larkhollow rule — activation. On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates exactly the privilege groups named in the decision — never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.

deliverables/rules.md:72:## 5. Six verification elements
deliverables/rules.md:81:| Initial appointment cycle is one year from effective date through the day before its first anniversary. Licence validity is required on decision date. If Washington licence expiry falls inside the cycle, track re-verification; it does not block initial activation. Record the condition due date as the expiry date. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **Check 1 — Licensure**, **“The cycle”** |
deliverables/rules.md:82:| Board lookup `lookup_date` is the office's own observation, not an external source reply; do not apply the verification usability window to it. A lookup on decision date is usable for that decision. | Written hospital policy | EXP, **“The Washington export's own columns”**; PROC, **8. Packet readiness**, **“The board lookup and the window”** |
deliverables/rules.md:95:| Compute gaps from the day after professional school ends. Treat declared entries as inclusive date ranges; an open end runs through the export date. Overlaps, part-time work, and training cover time. A gap is at least 30 consecutive uncovered days. Recompute the gap set when dates change. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **Check 2 — Experience and time gaps**; APP, **Sections D–F** |
deliverables/rules.md:105:### 5.5 Peer references
deliverables/rules.md:109:| The office sends the form directly to the named referee, who returns it directly. Applicant-carried references cannot be used. | Written hospital policy | REF, opening paragraph; PROC, **Check 4 — Professional peer references** |
deliverables/rules.md:110:| A referee qualifies only if all hold: direct work together within two years ending on signature date; same clinical discipline as applicant; and not a relative, spouse, or partner. Record an ineligible reply but do not count it. | Written hospital policy | REF, **Part 2 — completed by the referee**, **“Who may give a peer reference”**; PROC, **Check 4** |
deliverables/rules.md:111:| Reference currency is measured from signature date, not receipt date. It is current through the second anniversary of signature (presentation on or before that date); it can become stale while waiting. | Written hospital policy | REF, **“Currency”**; PROC, **Check 4 — Professional peer references**, **“when currency is measured”** |
deliverables/rules.md:113:| Two qualifying, current references satisfy the element. An otherwise open request does not hold a met element; retain its action until presentation, then close it as no longer needed. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **Check 4 — Professional peer references** |
deliverables/rules.md:126:### Professional practice / high-risk findings (outside the six verification-element keys)
deliverables/rules.md:133:**Project implementation mapping (not an additional hospital rule):** map licensure → `licensure`; work/affiliation history verification → `experience`; uncovered periods and their explanations → `gaps`; professional education/training → `education`; board certification and privilege support → `certification`; peer references → `references`. Keep professional-practice/high-risk findings in the companion ledger/action reporting; they are not a seventh schema element. This maps PROC, **3. The six checks** and **4. High-risk findings** to `snapshot.schema.json`, `applications[].elements`.
deliverables/rules.md:135:## 6. Readiness, decisions, and activation
deliverables/rules.md:139:| General verification usability window: completed on or after first application receipt and before decision date; no fixed day count. A later revision does not automatically invalidate all evidence. Reassess only entries affected by revision changes. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **8. Packet readiness**, **“The usability window”**; **2. Reconciliation** |
deliverables/rules.md:140:| A packet is presentable only when all six elements are resolved, no item is outstanding, no discrepancy is open, required verifications are usable, and readiness is tied to one named revision. An adverse finding remains in the record after its required authorized disposition clears its hold; do not treat every historical finding as a permanent blocker. A finding without its required disposition, an outstanding item, or an unresolved discrepancy still prevents presentation. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **8. Packet readiness**, **“What makes a packet presentable”**; AUTH, **Individual authority** |
deliverables/rules.md:141:| Readiness is not undone by a refused decision, withdrawal, or discontinuance. It is lost when an element reopens or a new revision arrives; preserve earlier readiness as history. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **8. Packet readiness**; **11. Re-entry** |
deliverables/rules.md:143:| Validate a decision using all five written conditions: authorized body/outcome; signatory held role on decision date; correct applicant and revision; presentable packet existed before decision date; valid outcome and required reason. Valid outcomes are approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, and not-recommended. Plain approval and positive recommendation carry no reason; approval-with-conditions, deferral, denial, and not-recommended require one. Do not accept a decision's own assertion of authority as proof. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **9. The committee protocol**, **“what makes a decision admissible”** and **“which outcomes carry a reason”**; AUTH, **Who may record what** and opening authority statement |
deliverables/rules.md:144:| A decision against a superseded revision remains history and cannot authorize the current revision. A second Governing Body decision for the same revision must identify the earlier decision it supersedes; otherwise it is inadmissible. Keep refused records and reasons. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **9. The committee protocol**, rules on superseded revisions and two decisions; AUTH, **Who may record what** |
deliverables/rules.md:146:| Only an admitted Governing Body approval activates privileges. Activate exactly the privileges named in that approval, on its effective date or decision date if no separate effective date is given. Never activate before then. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **10. Activation and the appointment cycle**; AUTH, **Who may record what** |
deliverables/rules.md:148:| Re-enter work for a new revision, new evidence/reclassification/corrected date, credential expiry/renewal, inadmissible or superseded decision, withdrawal, or discontinuance. Reopen only the affected work as specified and retain every prior occurrence. | Written hospital policy | PROC, **11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done** |
deliverables/rules.md:160:| Preserve detailed per-entry evidence and decision-to-revision linkage in a companion ledger because the schema's decision objects do not include revision, actor, body, date, outcome, or evidence fields. Do not squeeze unsupported fields into the schema. | Project implementation choice | `snapshot.schema.json`, `applications[].decisions[]` and `applications[].elements` definitions |
deliverables/rules.md:162:| Use schema validation plus separate semantic checks for cross-record joins, date arithmetic, status precedence, decision authority, and evidence consistency. Schema validation alone does not establish these business facts. | Project implementation choice | Existing `scripts/validate_snapshot.py` validates JSON Schema structure/formats; schema property definitions |
deliverables/rules.md:169:| Experience and competency | Verify relevant history; current competency is not determined by the office and does not make a privilege group unsupported. | Interview says experience may be “resolved after up to three attempts.” Do not implement this as a competency decision or an automatic resolution rule. | PROC, **Check 2 — Experience and time gaps**; PRIV, **How the office applies the table**, rule 7 |
deliverables/rules.md:170:| Referral/address completeness | Address condition is not assessable from this export. | Interview-level operational statements cannot supply missing addresses absent from the export. | EXP, **“What I do not export”** |
deliverables/rules.md:171:| Evidence schema detail | The schema is authoritative and unchanged; retain additional audit detail in the companion ledger. | Schema cannot encode all per-revision decision facts or source citations. | `snapshot.schema.json`, application and decision definitions |

office/export-notes.txt:1:How this office exports its credentialing records
office/export-notes.txt:2:Larkhollow Community Hospital · Medical Staff Office A note from the Medical Services Professional to whoever automates the initial-appointment file. Written 2026-03-16, alongside the first export.
office/export-notes.txt:3:I run the export from the credentialing database every few weeks and drop it in the shared folder, one sub-folder per export. Here is what you get, what the columns mean, and the three or four things that catch people out.
office/export-notes.txt:4:The export date is the clock
office/export-notes.txt:5:Every batch folder has a README.md that says the export date and the window it covers. That date is the clock for everything in the folder: nothing in a batch happened after its export date. Work the batch as if today were the export date. Do not use the real date you run your tool, and do not carry today's date into an arithmetic that a batch is supposed to settle.
office/export-notes.txt:6:The three exports are 2026-03-16, 2026-04-20 and 2026-05-18. The first one covers everything on file up to and including 2026-03-15, however far back it goes — one application here was first received in 2024. The second and third cover only what changed since the previous one.
office/export-notes.txt:7:The caseload at an export date is every application file the office has received up to that date, however that file ended. A withdrawn or discontinued file stays in the caseload with its final status; a later batch never removes a file, it only adds to what is known about it.
office/export-notes.txt:9:I never go back and edit an export. If an applicant corrects something, a new revision of the application appears in a later batch and the old one stays exactly where it was. If a board sends a corrected reply, the corrected reply is a new row and the old row stays. If a committee decides something twice, there are two decision records.
office/export-notes.txt:12:Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
office/export-notes.txt:31:	verification-replies.csv
office/export-notes.txt:33:	verification-attempts.csv
office/export-notes.txt:37:	peer-reference-replies.csv
office/export-notes.txt:38:	one completed reference form that came back
office/export-notes.txt:40:	one letter, memo or decision record, with the path to the document
office/export-notes.txt:49:	decisions/
office/export-notes.txt:52:A file with only a header row means the export ran and there was nothing in that window. That is not the same as a missing file, and it is not an error.
office/export-notes.txt:53:Dates, blanks and columns
office/export-notes.txt:55:* An empty cell means I hold no value for that field. It does not mean zero, it does not mean "no", and it does not mean the answer is unknown-but-probably-fine. Two blanks carry a specific meaning and you should learn them:
office/export-notes.txt:56:   * a blank to_date in declared-history.csv means the entry is current, running to the export date — not that the end date is missing;
office/export-notes.txt:57:   * a blank expiry_date in certification-replies.csv means the certificate does not expire — some older certificates are time-unlimited.
office/export-notes.txt:62:2. The Washington board export carries no practitioner identifier. It never has. I join it to an application on lastname, firstname, middlename and birthyear. I have checked that no two rows in any one export share those four values, so the join gives you at most one row. An applicant with no row in that file holds no Washington credential. The absence is the answer, not a data problem.
office/export-notes.txt:63:3. A referee with no row in peer-reference-replies.csv has not replied. Silence produces no record. You can see it only by looking at the requests in verification-attempts.csv and finding no reply against them.
office/export-notes.txt:64:The Washington export's own columns
office/export-notes.txt:69:The first export carries the board's whole file for our county — 435 rows — so you can see what an ordinary population looks like. The second and third carry only a re-lookup of the practitioners whose files are open, because that is all I re-run.
office/export-notes.txt:72:In the board's population, action against a credential is rare. In the 435-row export you have: 431 rows say No, 3 say Yes, and 1 says Pending. That is 0.69% Yes and 0.23% Pending, and it is the shape of the real thing — the overwhelming majority of licensed practitioners have a clean board record, and any tool that expects otherwise will be wrong almost every time it fires.
office/export-notes.txt:73:The applicants in these batches are a different matter, and deliberately so. This is a teaching set. I have put every situation the procedure has a rule for into these three exports on purpose, so the run has something to exercise: a restricted licence, an unexplained gap, a school that closed, a referee who never answers, a certificate that lapsed, a decision against the wrong revision. A real nine weeks of intake would be far quieter than this. Do not read the applicant set as a base rate. Read it as a checklist that happens to be shaped like a caseload.
office/export-notes.txt:75:What I do not export
office/export-notes.txt:76:My own queue, my own statuses and my own conclusions. This export is the evidence, not my reading of it. What is complete, what is outstanding, what is presentable and what is owed to whom is the work — it is not in the folder, and it should not be.
office/export-notes.txt:77:Referee addresses. The export carries no address column for peer referees. The working-address half of completeness condition 7 is checked by my office outside the export, so a run assesses condition 7 on the named referees alone and records the address check as not assessable from the export — neither met nor failed.

def _parse_decisions(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    out = []
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            continue
        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
            if "/decisions/" not in f"/{path}" or not content:
                continue
            f = _fields(content)
            if not f.get("decision id"):
                continue
            f["__ref"] = _document_ref(batch, doc)
            f["__content"] = content
            out.append(f)
    return out


def _decision_conditions(d: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read explicitly listed condition/due pairs from a decision record."""
    content = d.get("__content", "")
    section = re.search(r"^\*\*Conditions:\*\*[ \t]*\r?\n(.*?)(?=^##\s|\Z)", content, re.M | re.S)
    lines = section.group(1).splitlines() if section else []
    result = []
    for line in lines:
        item = re.match(r"\s*[-*]\s+(.+?)\s+[—–-]\s+due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$", line, re.I)
        if item and _parse_date(item.group(2)):
            result.append({"condition": item.group(1).strip(), "due": item.group(2)})
    # Older records may place a single explicit due-dated condition in Reason.
    if not result:
        for item in (d.get("reason") or "").split(";"):
            match = re.match(r"\s*(.*?)\s+due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$", item, re.I)
            if match and _parse_date(match.group(2)):
                result.append({"condition": match.group(1).strip(), "due": match.group(2)})
    return result


def _terminal_status(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, as_of: date) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, Any] | None]:
    """Find explicit applicant withdrawal or roster-authorized discontinuance."""
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            continue
        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
            if not content:
                continue
            fields = _fields(content)
            if fields.get("application") != app_id:
                continue
            if "/letters/" in f"/{path}" and re.search(r"\bI am withdrawing my application\b", content, re.I):
                when = _parse_date(fields.get("date"))
                if when and when <= as_of:
                    return "withdrawn", _document_ref(batch, doc)
    for disposition in _dispositions(ledger, app_id, "1", as_of):
        content = disposition["content"]
        if re.search(r"\bDiscontinue the application\b", content, re.I) and not re.search(r"\bDo not discontinue the application\b", content, re.I):
            return "discontinued", disposition["ref"]
    return None, None


def _cycle_end(effective: date) -> date:
    year = effective.year + 1
    anniversary = effective.replace(year=year, day=min(effective.day, calendar.monthrange(year, effective.month)[1]))
    return anniversary - timedelta(days=1)

The evaluator reports rule-mapped evidence states only. It does not admit
committee decisions, make clinical judgments, activate privileges, or create
snapshots.

def _parse_date(value: Any) -> date | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        return None
    try:
        return date.fromisoformat(value)
    except ValueError:
        return None


def _has_positive_accreditation(text: Any) -> bool:
    normalized = str(text or "").casefold().replace("–", "-").replace("—", "-")
    if re.search(r"\b(?:not|non|un)\s*-?\s*accredited\b", normalized):
        return False
    if re.search(r"\baccreditation\s+(?:not verified|unknown|unverified|not established)\b", normalized):
        return False
    return "accredited" in normalized or "accreditation confirmed" in normalized


def _anniversary(day: date, years: int) -> date:
    year = day.year + years
    return day.replace(year=year, day=min(day.day, calendar.monthrange(year, day.month)[1]))


def _subtract_years(day: date, years: int) -> date:
    year = day.year - years
    return day.replace(year=year, day=min(day.day, calendar.monthrange(year, day.month)[1]))


def _row_records(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date) -> list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]:
    result = []
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        batch_date = _parse_date(batch.get("export_date"))
        if batch_date is None or batch_date > as_of:
            continue
        for record in batch.get("records", []):
            result.append((batch, record))
    return result


def _source_ref(batch: dict[str, Any], record: dict[str, Any], document_path: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ref = {
        "batch_id": batch.get("batch_id"),
        "filename": record.get("filename"),
        "row_number": record.get("row_number"),
        "stable_key": record.get("stable_key"),
    }
    if document_path:
        ref["document_path"] = document_path
    return ref


class _Element:
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
        self.evidence: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.observations: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        self.problems: set[str] = set()

    def cite(self, batch: dict[str, Any], record: dict[str, Any], document_path: str | None = None) -> None:
        ref = _source_ref(batch, record, document_path)
        if ref not in self.evidence:
            self.evidence.append(ref)

    def note(self, code: str, message: str, evidence: Iterable[dict[str, Any]] = ()) -> None:
        self.problems.add(code)
        entry = {"code": code, "message": message}
        cited = list(evidence)
        if cited:
            entry["evidence"] = cited
        if entry not in self.observations:
            self.observations.append(entry)

    def finish(self, forced_state: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        if forced_state:
            state = forced_state
        else:
            # Observation codes remain detailed in the companion result; this
            # table maps them to the schema's coarser state vocabulary.
            state_codes = {
                "return-incomplete": {"unexplained_gap"},
                "discrepancy": {
                    "conflicting_source_responses", "unresolved_discrepancy",
                    "conflicting_certification_replies", "certification_identity_mismatch",
                    "undeclared_washington_license", "declared_certification_not_confirmed",
                },
                "routed-to-clinical-director": {"gap_disposition_pending"},
                "eligibility-question": {"threshold_eligibility_question"},
                "finding": {
                    "licensure_finding", "washington_license_not_current",
                    "washington_practice_license_missing",
                    "unsupported_requested_privilege",
                },
                "outstanding": {
                    "no_entries_to_verify", "missing_history_date", "missing_entry_id",
                    "professional_school_end_missing", "inadmissible_source",
                    "unusable_verification_date", "verification_outstanding", "unresolved_verification_outcome",
                    "incomplete_verification_content",
                    "accreditation_not_recorded", "gap_disposition_pending",
                    "licence_verification_outstanding", "inadmissible_license_source", "invalid_license_lookup_date",
                    "inadmissible_certification_source", "unusable_certification_date", "certification_verification_outstanding",
                    "no_privilege_request", "unknown_privilege_code", "board_action_requires_detail",
                    "privilege_support_not_established", "reference_outstanding", "reference_date_unusable",
                    "reference_not_countable", "two_references_not_established", "reference_channel_unverified",
                },
            }
            for state_name, codes in state_codes.items():
                if self.problems.intersection(codes):
                    self.problems.add(state_name)
            for candidate in (
                "return-incomplete",
                "discrepancy",
                "routed-to-clinical-director",
                "finding",
                "outstanding",
                "eligibility-question",
            ):
                if candidate in self.problems:
                    state = candidate
                    break
            else:
                state = "resolved"
        assert state in ELEMENT_STATES
        return {
            "state": state,
            "evidence": self.evidence,
            "rule_refs": POLICY[self.name],
            "observations": self.observations,
        }


def _doc_index(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date, application_id: str) -> list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]:
    output = []
    for batch, record in _row_records(ledger, as_of):
        values = record.get("values", {})
        if record.get("filename") != "correspondence.csv" or values.get("application_id") != application_id:
            continue
        path = values.get("document_path")
        for source_batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
            if source_batch.get("batch_id") != batch.get("batch_id"):
                continue
            document = next((d for d in source_batch.get("documents", []) if d.get("path") == path), None)
            if document is not None:
                doc_date_match = re.search(r"^\*\*Date:\*\*\s*(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})", document.get("content", ""), re.MULTILINE)
                doc_date = _parse_date(doc_date_match.group(1)) if doc_date_match else None
                if doc_date is None or doc_date <= as_of:
                    output.append((batch, record, document))
    return output


def _entry_replies(
    rows: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]], application_id: str, entry_id: str, element: str
) -> list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]:
    return [
        (batch, record)
        for batch, record in rows
        if record.get("filename") == "verification-replies.csv"
        and record.get("values", {}).get("application_id") == application_id
        and record.get("values", {}).get("entry_id") == entry_id
        and record.get("values", {}).get("element") == element
    ]


def _source_class(element: str, values: dict[str, Any], docs: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]) -> tuple[str, str]:
    received = str(values.get("received_from") or "").strip().casefold()
    organization = str(values.get("attester_organization") or "").strip().casefold()
    context = str(values.get("notes") or "").casefold()
    doc_text = "\n".join(d.get("content", "") for _, _, d in docs).casefold()

    if "applicant" in received:
        return "inadmissible", "Applicant-delivered primary-source material is not an acceptable verification source."

    if element == "education-and-training":
        if received.startswith(("registrar's office", "dean's office", "graduate medical education office", "programme director")):
            return "primary", "Listed primary education/training source."
        if any(term in received or term in organization for term in (
            "ecfmg", "federation credentials verification service", "fcvs",
            "american medical association physician profile", "ama physician profile",
            "american osteopathic association physician profile", "aoa physician profile",
            "national student clearinghouse",
        )):
            return "designated-equivalent", "Listed designated equivalent education/training source."
        if received.startswith("medical staff office") and any(term in (context + "\n" + doc_text) for term in ("school closed", "programme closed", "program closed", "school has closed")):
            reason_present = any(term in (context + "\n" + doc_text) for term in ("no designated equivalent", "no equivalent source", "does not exist", "closed and no"))
            if reason_present:
                return "secondary-impossibility", "Closed school/programme exception is documented in the source notes or indexed record."
        return "inadmissible", "Source is not identified in the closed education/training source table."

    if element == "affiliation-and-employment":
        if received.startswith(("medical staff office", "human resources", "authorized administrator", "employer's human resources")):
            return "primary", "Listed primary affiliation/employment source."
        if any(term in received for term in ("credentials verification organization", "credentials verification organisation", "cvo")):
            if organization and (organization in received or organization in context):
                return "designated-equivalent", "CVO is identified as acting for the affiliation/employer."
            return "inadmissible", "CVO response does not identify the affiliation/employer it acted for."
        if received.startswith("medical staff office") and any(term in (context + "\n" + doc_text) for term in ("employer dissolved", "employer has dissolved", "no successor")):
            return "secondary-impossibility", "Dissolved-employer exception is documented."
        return "inadmissible", "Source is not identified in the closed affiliation/employment source table."

    return "inadmissible", "No source rule is defined for this element."


def _reply_is_usable(values: dict[str, Any], first_received: date, as_of: date) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    received = _parse_date(values.get("received_date"))
    if received is None:
        return False, "Verification has no valid received_date."
    if received > as_of:
        return False, "Verification was received after the requested export date."
    if received < first_received:

office/privilege-criteria.txt-75-2. A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-76-3. An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.

Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-78-5. PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-79-6. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. The office raises it to the Clinical Director, who decides whether the application is discontinued. The office does not discontinue an application. The office raises it on what has been verified at the export date: while nothing yet verified supports any requested group, the question stands with the Clinical Director, and it is withdrawn without a disposition when a later verification supports the request.
office/privilege-criteria.txt:80:7. The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. Current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the office (the manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8), and it is one of the elements this procedure does not handle. Whether a group is supported is decided by rules 1 to 6 alone; the current-experience requirement travels with the packet for the committee and never makes a group unsupported.
office/privilege-criteria.txt:81:Whether a supported request should be granted is not settled here. That is the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff's recommendation and the Governing Body's decision.
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-47-Six elements are verified in this procedure: licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. The manual numbers seventeen essential credentialing elements in Section 6, Subsection 4. Of the other eleven, nine are handled by the office outside this procedure, as stated above; current competency is the clinical leadership's, not the office's; and the manual's conditions-and-release form is replaced by our own Authorization and Release, which is part of intake in this procedure.
office/procedure-extract.txt-48-What counts as a verification at all
office/procedure-extract.txt-49-The manual, Section 1, defines primary source verification as
office/procedure-extract.txt-50-"Verifying a credential from the original source"
office/procedure-extract.txt-51-and Section 6, Subsection 1 rules out two things we see constantly:
office/procedure-extract.txt:52:"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
office/procedure-extract.txt-53-"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
office/procedure-extract.txt-54-A reply that reached us through the applicant is not a verification, however genuine the document looks, however clear the letterhead, however real the registrar's signature. It goes in the file as received and the request stays open.
office/procedure-extract.txt-55-A designated equivalent source is acceptable in place of the original. The manual leaves each of its lists open — Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends
office/procedure-extract.txt-56-"etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications"
office/procedure-extract.txt-57-and element 5 ends
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-81-Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
office/procedure-extract.txt-82-The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
office/procedure-extract.txt-83-Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
office/procedure-extract.txt-84-Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
office/procedure-extract.txt-85-"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
office/procedure-extract.txt:86:The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
office/procedure-extract.txt-87-Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
office/procedure-extract.txt-88-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
office/procedure-extract.txt-89-"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
office/procedure-extract.txt-90-"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
office/procedure-extract.txt-91-Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-105-The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
office/procedure-extract.txt-106-"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
office/procedure-extract.txt-107-Check 4 — Professional peer references
office/procedure-extract.txt-108-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
office/procedure-extract.txt-109-"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
office/procedure-extract.txt:110:"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
office/procedure-extract.txt-111-"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
office/procedure-extract.txt-112-"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
office/procedure-extract.txt:113:Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
office/procedure-extract.txt-114-Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
office/procedure-extract.txt:115:* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
office/procedure-extract.txt-116-* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
office/procedure-extract.txt-117-* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-118-Currency, from Section 8:
office/procedure-extract.txt-119-"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
office/procedure-extract.txt-120-The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt:121:Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
office/procedure-extract.txt-122-Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
office/procedure-extract.txt-123-Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-124-Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-125-Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
office/procedure-extract.txt-126-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-130-On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
office/procedure-extract.txt-131-"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
office/procedure-extract.txt-132-"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-133-and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
office/procedure-extract.txt-134-"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
office/procedure-extract.txt:135:Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-136-Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
office/procedure-extract.txt-137-Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
office/procedure-extract.txt-138-"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-139-"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-140-"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-141-The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
office/procedure-extract.txt:142:Check 6 — The committee decision
office/procedure-extract.txt-143-Covered in sections 8 and 9.
office/procedure-extract.txt-144-4. High-risk findings
office/procedure-extract.txt-145-The manual, Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-146-"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
office/procedure-extract.txt-147-"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-173-The manual, Section 12:
office/procedure-extract.txt-174-"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
office/procedure-extract.txt-175-and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
office/procedure-extract.txt-176-"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
office/procedure-extract.txt-177-The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
office/procedure-extract.txt:178:Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
office/procedure-extract.txt:179:Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:180:Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
office/procedure-extract.txt:181:For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
office/procedure-extract.txt:182:A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
office/procedure-extract.txt:183:Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-184-9. The committee protocol
office/procedure-extract.txt-185-The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
office/procedure-extract.txt-186-"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
office/procedure-extract.txt-187-and the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
office/procedure-extract.txt-188-"proposes a recommendation through the clinical director (CD) and the chief executive officer (CEO) or their designee to the Governing Body"
office/procedure-extract.txt-189-Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-190-"The GB or a delegated GB committee retains the final authority to grant, renew, or deny privileges after considering the recommendations of the medical staff"
office/procedure-extract.txt-191-Section 12, on who may record what:
office/procedure-extract.txt-192-"All signatories should utilize a "recommend" selection, with only the Chair of the GB or their designee using the "approval" selection."
office/procedure-extract.txt-193-A recommendation is not an approval. A record from the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff that carries the word "approved" is still a recommendation, because those bodies cannot approve. Only the Governing Body chair, or the designee named in authority-roster.md, records an approval.
office/procedure-extract.txt:194:Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible. All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
office/procedure-extract.txt-195-1. the body is one that may record that outcome;
office/procedure-extract.txt:196:2. the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
office/procedure-extract.txt:197:3. the decision names the same applicant and the same application revision as the presentable packet;
office/procedure-extract.txt:198:4. a presentable packet existed for that revision before the decision date;
office/procedure-extract.txt-199-5. the outcome is one of approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, not recommended, and every outcome other than a plain approval carries a reason.
office/procedure-extract.txt:200:A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:201:Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision. It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
office/procedure-extract.txt:202:Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision. A second decision for the same application revision is admissible only when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
office/procedure-extract.txt:203:Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision. recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
office/procedure-extract.txt-204-Larkhollow rule — deferral. A deferral names the information it waits for. The office chases exactly that, and the file does not advance while it waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt-205-10. Activation and the appointment cycle
office/procedure-extract.txt-206-The manual, Section 5:
office/procedure-extract.txt-207-"The provider cannot provide patient care services until the practitioner has been approved for their next appointment and privilege cycle."
office/procedure-extract.txt-208-and Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-209-"The GB needs to approve a provider's privileges and/or appointment on or before the"
office/procedure-extract.txt-210-expiry date, to prevent a lapse; and a later start date is permitted when the body records it:
office/procedure-extract.txt-211-"Yes, if the GB makes the notation in their final notes when they sign off on the signature pages in Virtual Committee."
office/procedure-extract.txt:212:Larkhollow rule — activation. On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates exactly the privilege groups named in the decision — never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.
office/procedure-extract.txt-213-Larkhollow rule — approve with conditions. An approval with conditions activates the approved privilege groups on the normal rule above, and records each condition as a monitored condition with its own due date. A condition is satisfied only by a record naming it. A condition still unmet on its due date becomes a finding to the Clinical Director.
office/procedure-extract.txt-214-Monitored conditions do not block activation. A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
office/procedure-extract.txt-215-11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
office/procedure-extract.txt-216-The manual, Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-217-"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-219-A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.
office/procedure-extract.txt-220-Larkhollow rule — the five re-entry triggers, and what each affects:
office/procedure-extract.txt-221-What arrives
office/procedure-extract.txt-222-	What it affects
office/procedure-extract.txt-223-	A new application revision
office/procedure-extract.txt:224:	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
office/procedure-extract.txt-225-	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
office/procedure-extract.txt:226:	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
office/procedure-extract.txt-227-	A credential expires or is renewed
office/procedure-extract.txt-228-	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
office/procedure-extract.txt:229:	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
office/procedure-extract.txt-230-	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
office/procedure-extract.txt-231-	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
office/procedure-extract.txt-232-	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
office/procedure-extract.txt-233-	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

office/privilege-criteria.txt-70-	Completion of an accredited orthopaedic surgery residency, 60 months

office/privilege-criteria.txt:74:1. A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-75-2. A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-76-3. An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.
office/privilege-criteria.txt:77:4. Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-78-5. PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.
office/privilege-criteria.txt-79-6. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. office/privilege-criteria.txt:80:7. The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. office/procedure-extract.txt-47-Six elements are verified in this procedure: licensure, experience, time gaps, professional education and post-graduate training, board certification, and professional peer references. The manual numbers seventeen essential credentialing elements in Section 6, Subsection 4. Of the other eleven, nine are handled by the office outside this procedure, as stated above; current competency is the clinical leadership's, not the office's; and the manual's conditions-and-release form is replaced by our own Authorization and Release, which is part of intake in this procedure.
office/procedure-extract.txt-48-What counts as a verification at all
office/procedure-extract.txt-49-The manual, Section 1, defines primary source verification as
office/procedure-extract.txt-50-"Verifying a credential from the original source"
office/procedure-extract.txt-51-and Section 6, Subsection 1 rules out two things we see constantly:
office/procedure-extract.txt:52:"Primary source verifications received directly from the applicant cannot be used."
office/procedure-extract.txt-53-"Copies of a diploma, license, registration, etc., in place of verifications are unacceptable."
office/procedure-extract.txt-54-A reply that reached us through the applicant is not a verification, however genuine the document looks, however clear the letterhead, however real the registrar's signature. It goes in the file as received and the request stays open.
office/procedure-extract.txt-55-A designated equivalent source is acceptable in place of the original. The manual leaves each of its lists open — Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2 ends
office/procedure-extract.txt-56-"etc., as long as the source is a designated equivalent source for education and training verifications"
office/procedure-extract.txt-57-and element 5 ends

office/procedure-extract.txt-81-Larkhollow rule — full and unrestricted. A licence is not full and unrestricted when the board's record or the board's reply shows probation, supervision, a monitoring agreement, a practice limitation, a suspension, a stipulated condition or a surrender. A licence in any of those states is a finding and goes to the Clinical Director with its evidence. It is not the office's judgment whether the restriction matters.
office/procedure-extract.txt-82-The element's state is finding from the day the restriction is seen and stays finding on every later record of that revision, including after the Clinical Director's disposition ends the hold on the file. The disposition ends the wait; it does not turn a finding into a clean element. resolved is for an element with nothing to weigh.
office/procedure-extract.txt-83-Larkhollow rule — a National Provider Identifier is not a licence. It identifies a practitioner for billing. It says nothing about whether anybody is licensed. An applicant who declares an identifier in place of a licence has declared no licence.
office/procedure-extract.txt-84-Larkhollow rule — the cycle. An initial appointment at Larkhollow runs one year, matching the manual's Section 12:
office/procedure-extract.txt-85-"For IHS, initial appointments are one year long, and reappointments are two years long, regardless of accrediting body medical staff standards or medical staff bylaws."
office/procedure-extract.txt:86:The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
office/procedure-extract.txt-87-Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
office/procedure-extract.txt-88-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
office/procedure-extract.txt-89-"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
office/procedure-extract.txt-90-"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
office/procedure-extract.txt-91-Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-105-The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
office/procedure-extract.txt-106-"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
office/procedure-extract.txt-107-Check 4 — Professional peer references
office/procedure-extract.txt-108-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
office/procedure-extract.txt-109-"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
office/procedure-extract.txt:110:"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
office/procedure-extract.txt-111-"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
office/procedure-extract.txt-112-"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
office/procedure-extract.txt:113:Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
office/procedure-extract.txt-114-Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
office/procedure-extract.txt:115:* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
office/procedure-extract.txt-116-* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
office/procedure-extract.txt-117-* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-118-Currency, from Section 8:
office/procedure-extract.txt-119-"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
office/procedure-extract.txt-120-The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt:121:Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
office/procedure-extract.txt-122-Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
office/procedure-extract.txt-123-Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-124-Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-125-Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
office/procedure-extract.txt-126-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
