office/procedure-extract.txt-130-On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
office/procedure-extract.txt-131-"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
office/procedure-extract.txt-132-"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-133-and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
office/procedure-extract.txt-134-"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
office/procedure-extract.txt:135:Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-136-Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
office/procedure-extract.txt-137-Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
office/procedure-extract.txt-138-"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-139-"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-140-"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-141-The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.

office/procedure-extract.txt-143-Covered in sections 8 and 9.
office/procedure-extract.txt-144-4. High-risk findings
office/procedure-extract.txt-145-The manual, Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-146-"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
office/procedure-extract.txt-147-"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-173-The manual, Section 12:
office/procedure-extract.txt-174-"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
office/procedure-extract.txt-175-and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
office/procedure-extract.txt-176-"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
office/procedure-extract.txt-177-The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
office/procedure-extract.txt:178:Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
office/procedure-extract.txt:179:Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:180:Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
office/procedure-extract.txt:181:For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
office/procedure-extract.txt:182:A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
office/procedure-extract.txt:183:Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-184-9. The committee protocol
office/procedure-extract.txt-185-The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
office/procedure-extract.txt-186-"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
office/procedure-extract.txt-187-and the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
office/procedure-extract.txt-188-"proposes a recommendation through the clinical director (CD) and the chief executive officer (CEO) or their designee to the Governing Body"
office/procedure-extract.txt-189-Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-190-"The GB or a delegated GB committee retains the final authority to grant, renew, or deny privileges after considering the recommendations of the medical staff"
office/procedure-extract.txt-191-Section 12, on who may record what:
office/procedure-extract.txt-192-"All signatories should utilize a "recommend" selection, with only the Chair of the GB or their designee using the "approval" selection."
office/procedure-extract.txt-193-A recommendation is not an approval. A record from the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff that carries the word "approved" is still a recommendation, because those bodies cannot approve. Only the Governing Body chair, or the designee named in authority-roster.md, records an approval.
office/procedure-extract.txt:194:Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible. All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
office/procedure-extract.txt-195-1. the body is one that may record that outcome;
office/procedure-extract.txt:196:2. the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
office/procedure-extract.txt:197:3. the decision names the same applicant and the same application revision as the presentable packet;
office/procedure-extract.txt:198:4. a presentable packet existed for that revision before the decision date;
office/procedure-extract.txt-199-5. the outcome is one of approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, not recommended, and every outcome other than a plain approval carries a reason.
office/procedure-extract.txt:200:A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:201:Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision. It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
office/procedure-extract.txt:202:Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision. A second decision for the same application revision is admissible only when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
office/procedure-extract.txt:203:Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision. recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
office/procedure-extract.txt-204-Larkhollow rule — deferral. A deferral names the information it waits for. The office chases exactly that, and the file does not advance while it waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt-205-10. Activation and the appointment cycle
office/procedure-extract.txt-206-The manual, Section 5:
office/procedure-extract.txt-207-"The provider cannot provide patient care services until the practitioner has been approved for their next appointment and privilege cycle."
office/procedure-extract.txt-208-and Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-209-"The GB needs to approve a provider's privileges and/or appointment on or before the"
office/procedure-extract.txt-210-expiry date, to prevent a lapse; and a later start date is permitted when the body records it:
office/procedure-extract.txt-211-"Yes, if the GB makes the notation in their final notes when they sign off on the signature pages in Virtual Committee."
office/procedure-extract.txt:212:Larkhollow rule — activation. On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates exactly the privilege groups named in the decision — never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.
office/procedure-extract.txt-213-Larkhollow rule — approve with conditions. An approval with conditions activates the approved privilege groups on the normal rule above, and records each condition as a monitored condition with its own due date. A condition is satisfied only by a record naming it. A condition still unmet on its due date becomes a finding to the Clinical Director.
office/procedure-extract.txt-214-Monitored conditions do not block activation. A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
office/procedure-extract.txt-215-11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
office/procedure-extract.txt-216-The manual, Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-217-"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-219-A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.

office/procedure-extract.txt-221-What arrives
office/procedure-extract.txt-222-	What it affects
office/procedure-extract.txt-223-	A new application revision
office/procedure-extract.txt:224:	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
office/procedure-extract.txt-225-	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
office/procedure-extract.txt:226:	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
office/procedure-extract.txt-227-	A credential expires or is renewed
office/procedure-extract.txt-228-	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
office/procedure-extract.txt:229:	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
office/procedure-extract.txt-230-	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
office/procedure-extract.txt-231-	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
office/procedure-extract.txt-232-	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
office/procedure-extract.txt-233-	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

office/procedure-extract.txt:86:The cycle starts on the date the appointment takes effect and ends one year later minus one day, so a cycle starting 2026-05-01 ends 2027-04-30. The Washington licence must be valid on the decision date. If it expires inside the cycle, that is not a denial and it is not a pass: it is recorded as a monitored condition with a re-verification due date set before the expiry date, and it does not block activation. If the re-verification fails, the file re-opens. The due date recorded on the condition is the licence's expiry date itself; "before" says when the re-verification must be complete, not what the recorded date is.
office/procedure-extract.txt-87-Check 2 — Experience and time gaps
office/procedure-extract.txt-88-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 3:
office/procedure-extract.txt-89-"At the initial appointment, relevant experience (affiliations, work history, and military) for at least the most recent five years for work history and the most recent five years for affiliation history"
office/procedure-extract.txt-90-"or as far back as necessary per any conflicting information or suspicious indicators—to assess current competency is verified."
office/procedure-extract.txt-91-Five years is a floor, not a ceiling. Conflicting information takes us further back.
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-105-The manual also states the boundary this check does not cross, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 2:
office/procedure-extract.txt-106-"obtaining a degree and postgraduate training does not automatically confer a license to practice"
office/procedure-extract.txt-107-Check 4 — Professional peer references
office/procedure-extract.txt-108-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 11:
office/procedure-extract.txt-109-"IHS policy requires the collection of at least two peer references at the initial appointment. The"
office/procedure-extract.txt:110:"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
office/procedure-extract.txt-111-"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
office/procedure-extract.txt-112-"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
office/procedure-extract.txt:113:Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
office/procedure-extract.txt-114-Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
office/procedure-extract.txt:115:* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
office/procedure-extract.txt-116-* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
office/procedure-extract.txt-117-* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-118-Currency, from Section 8:
office/procedure-extract.txt-119-"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
office/procedure-extract.txt-120-The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt:121:Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
office/procedure-extract.txt-122-Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
office/procedure-extract.txt-123-Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-124-Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
office/procedure-extract.txt-125-Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
office/procedure-extract.txt-126-The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-130-On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
office/procedure-extract.txt-131-"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
office/procedure-extract.txt-132-"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-133-and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
office/procedure-extract.txt-134-"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
office/procedure-extract.txt:135:Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-136-Larkhollow rule — name the unsupported subset. When some requested privileges are supported and some are not, the finding names the ones that are not. It does not reject the whole request.
office/procedure-extract.txt-137-Larkhollow rule — no supporting certification at all. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested privilege group, this is an eligibility question, not a finding. The manual, Section 9:
office/procedure-extract.txt-138-"Threshold eligibility criteria are in place and consistently applied to each new applicant for medical staff membership and privileges."
office/procedure-extract.txt-139-"Do not accept applications for membership or clinical privileges from applicants who do not meet privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-140-"the clinical director will be consulted regarding discontinuing the application because the applicant doesn't meet the privileging"
office/procedure-extract.txt-141-The office raises it. The Clinical Director decides whether the application is discontinued.
office/procedure-extract.txt:142:Check 6 — The committee decision
office/procedure-extract.txt-143-Covered in sections 8 and 9.
office/procedure-extract.txt-144-4. High-risk findings
office/procedure-extract.txt-145-The manual, Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-146-"A high-risk credentialing finding is identified as an applicant answering yes to any professional practice questions in "Table 1. Credentialing High-Risk Table" on an application."
office/procedure-extract.txt-147-"In addition, if any documents or verifications supporting the application illustrate that the applicant should have answered yes to a professional practice question but did not, the applicant is contacted to confirm the response."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-173-The manual, Section 12:
office/procedure-extract.txt-174-"It is recommended that every file be audited before it goes through review."
office/procedure-extract.txt-175-and Section 8, on how long a verification stays good:
office/procedure-extract.txt-176-"Most of these verifications are required by accrediting organizations to be verified AT the time of appointment, the time between when the application is received and when it's reviewed."
office/procedure-extract.txt-177-The manual gave a fixed number once and removed it: its own change log for Version 5.0 records "Section 8: Removed 120-day expiration of primary source verifications."
office/procedure-extract.txt:178:Larkhollow rule — the usability window. A verification is usable when it was completed on or after the date this application was first received and before the decision date. There is no day count. The anchor is the date revision 1 arrived, not the date of the current revision, so a later revision does not by itself void every verification already completed — what a revision invalidates is decided entry by entry, by reading what the revision actually changed. Peer references carry the additional two-year signature rule in check 4, which is stricter and wins where the two disagree.
office/procedure-extract.txt:179:Larkhollow rule — the board lookup and the window. A board lookup is the office's own check of the state board's public record on a day of the office's choosing, not a reply from a source, so the usability window is not applied to it: a lookup run on the decision day is usable for that decision. The date a packet became presentable is the date the last verification reply it needed was received; the lookup does not set it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:180:Larkhollow rule — what makes a packet presentable. Every one of the six elements resolved, no element outstanding, no discrepancy open, every verification inside the usability window, and the packet bound to one named application revision. Readiness is computed from the element statuses, not from anybody's recollection that the file looked finished.
office/procedure-extract.txt:181:For readiness, resolved means the element has nothing left to verify. An element carrying a finding is resolved in that sense once its evidence is with the Clinical Director — a licensure finding once the Clinical Director's disposition is on file, a certification finding on part of the request at once — and the packet is presented with the finding on it. An eligibility question, a gap awaiting the Clinical Director's disposition, an open discrepancy, an item returned to the applicant and a high-risk finding without its disposition are not resolved: while any of them stands, the packet is not presentable.
office/procedure-extract.txt:182:A packet is a statement about one revision at one moment. If any element re-opens, readiness for that revision is gone, and the earlier readiness record stays in the file as history.
office/procedure-extract.txt:183:Readiness is a fact about the revision's elements and nothing else. A refused decision record does not undo it, and a withdrawn or discontinued file keeps the readiness its revision had: the office records what was ready, whatever the file did next. Only an element re-opening or a new revision changes it.
office/procedure-extract.txt-184-9. The committee protocol
office/procedure-extract.txt-185-The medical staff recommends; the Governing Body approves. The manual, Section 1:
office/procedure-extract.txt-186-"The Governing Body has the authority to grant, modify, or deny medical staff membership and clinical privileges to LPs"
office/procedure-extract.txt-187-and the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff
office/procedure-extract.txt-188-"proposes a recommendation through the clinical director (CD) and the chief executive officer (CEO) or their designee to the Governing Body"
office/procedure-extract.txt-189-Section 7:
office/procedure-extract.txt-190-"The GB or a delegated GB committee retains the final authority to grant, renew, or deny privileges after considering the recommendations of the medical staff"
office/procedure-extract.txt-191-Section 12, on who may record what:
office/procedure-extract.txt-192-"All signatories should utilize a "recommend" selection, with only the Chair of the GB or their designee using the "approval" selection."
office/procedure-extract.txt-193-A recommendation is not an approval. A record from the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff that carries the word "approved" is still a recommendation, because those bodies cannot approve. Only the Governing Body chair, or the designee named in authority-roster.md, records an approval.
office/procedure-extract.txt:194:Larkhollow rule — what makes a decision admissible. All five, checked against the roster and the packet and never against the record's own claim:
office/procedure-extract.txt-195-1. the body is one that may record that outcome;
office/procedure-extract.txt:196:2. the signatory held the named role on the decision date, per authority-roster.md;
office/procedure-extract.txt:197:3. the decision names the same applicant and the same application revision as the presentable packet;
office/procedure-extract.txt:198:4. a presentable packet existed for that revision before the decision date;
office/procedure-extract.txt-199-5. the outcome is one of approved, approved-with-conditions, deferred-pending-information, denied, recommended, not recommended, and every outcome other than a plain approval carries a reason.
office/procedure-extract.txt:200:A decision that fails any of these is not a decision. It is recorded as received, raised to the Medical Services Professional, and nothing activates on it.
office/procedure-extract.txt:201:Larkhollow rule — a decision against a superseded revision. It does not authorize the current revision. It stays in the file as history against the revision it named, and it is never deleted.
office/procedure-extract.txt:202:Larkhollow rule — two decisions for one revision. A second decision for the same application revision is admissible only when it names the earlier decision it supersedes. Without that reference it is a duplicate, it is inadmissible, and it is raised to the Medical Services Professional. The first decision continues to stand.
office/procedure-extract.txt:203:Larkhollow rule — which outcomes carry a reason, and what counts as a second decision. recommended is the positive outcome of a body that cannot approve (the Credentials Committee or the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff); like a plain approval it carries no reason, while not recommended carries one, as do approval-with-conditions, deferral and denial. The two-decisions rule above applies to a second decision of the same body for the same revision: a recommendation followed by the Governing Body's decision on the same revision is the normal sequence, not a duplicate, and a second recommendation is never a duplicate — so in practice it is a second Governing Body decision for the same revision that must name the earlier one it supersedes.
office/procedure-extract.txt-204-Larkhollow rule — deferral. A deferral names the information it waits for. The office chases exactly that, and the file does not advance while it waits.
office/procedure-extract.txt-205-10. Activation and the appointment cycle
office/procedure-extract.txt-206-The manual, Section 5:
office/procedure-extract.txt-207-"The provider cannot provide patient care services until the practitioner has been approved for their next appointment and privilege cycle."
office/procedure-extract.txt-208-and Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-209-"The GB needs to approve a provider's privileges and/or appointment on or before the"
office/procedure-extract.txt-210-expiry date, to prevent a lapse; and a later start date is permitted when the body records it:
office/procedure-extract.txt-211-"Yes, if the GB makes the notation in their final notes when they sign off on the signature pages in Virtual Committee."
office/procedure-extract.txt:212:Larkhollow rule — activation. On an admitted Governing Body approval, the office records the appointment and activates exactly the privilege groups named in the decision — never more, and never a group that was requested but not granted. Privileges become active on the effective date the decision records, or on the decision date when the decision records no separate effective date. Nothing is active before that day. The cycle end is computed as in check 1.
office/procedure-extract.txt-213-Larkhollow rule — approve with conditions. An approval with conditions activates the approved privilege groups on the normal rule above, and records each condition as a monitored condition with its own due date. A condition is satisfied only by a record naming it. A condition still unmet on its due date becomes a finding to the Clinical Director.
office/procedure-extract.txt-214-Monitored conditions do not block activation. A licence expiring inside the cycle, and a condition attached to an approval, are both tracked to their due dates while the privileges run.
office/procedure-extract.txt-215-11. Re-entry: when something lands on work already done
office/procedure-extract.txt-216-The manual, Section 15:
office/procedure-extract.txt-217-"The MSP must verify all expirables upon expiration and place the documentation in the file."
--
office/procedure-extract.txt-219-A file waiting for a committee is not frozen. Credentials go on expiring underneath it and we go on watching them.
office/procedure-extract.txt-220-Larkhollow rule — the five re-entry triggers, and what each affects:
office/procedure-extract.txt-221-What arrives
office/procedure-extract.txt-222-	What it affects
office/procedure-extract.txt-223-	A new application revision
office/procedure-extract.txt:224:	intake and completeness run again on the new revision; the prior revision stays in the file; any packet readiness bound to the prior revision is gone
office/procedure-extract.txt-225-	New evidence on an element — a reply, a reclassification, a corrected date
office/procedure-extract.txt:226:	that element re-opens; packet readiness is gone; other elements are untouched
office/procedure-extract.txt-227-	A credential expires or is renewed
office/procedure-extract.txt-228-	the licensure check re-runs on the new dates; a re-verification is placed in the file
office/procedure-extract.txt:229:	A decision that is not admissible, or that names a superseded revision
office/procedure-extract.txt-230-	nothing activates; the record is raised, kept, and never deleted
office/procedure-extract.txt-231-	A withdrawal by the applicant, or a discontinuation by the Clinical Director
office/procedure-extract.txt-232-	the file ends with the terminal reason recorded. It is never labelled appointed
office/procedure-extract.txt-233-	A re-entry adds an occurrence to the file. It does not overwrite the occurrence before it.

# Practitioner credentialing

Build a reusable Agent Skill that runs a medical staff office's initial-appointment credentialing file from application intake to recorded appointment and active privileges.

## Start

1. Read the [full task](https://docs.google.com/document/d/REDACTED/edit): it owns the scope, deliverables and acceptance requirements.
2. Create your own repository from [this starter](https://github.com/GitRollTraining/practitioner-credentialing) using **Use this template → Create a new repository**, then clone your copy and work there.

## Supplied files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `README.md` | Starting instructions and the full-task link. |
| `snapshot.schema.json` | The required shape of the per-batch snapshot your Skill writes. Validate every snapshot against it. Your implementation language and validation library are yours. |

You create the Skill, its implementation, your own checks and every output the task requires. Nothing here implements any part of the office's work.

## Before you work

**Interview rule.** You conduct the stakeholder interview yourself, and the questions are yours. Do not connect a coding agent or any other AI to the interview to run, script, or automate it. The interview transcript is assessed together with the code; a project whose interview was run by an agent is not scored.

- Export your interview as the original Work Sim Markdown, save one final complete file per session under `interviews/`, and commit and push it with your code. Do not rewrite the export. If the export is unavailable, contact the facilitator.
- No runtime is supplied. Choose the dependencies your Skill needs and document how to install and run it.
- Complete the program's coding-session capture setup in the course before assessed work, and confirm your session is being captured after your first meaningful commit. Ask the facilitator to repair missing capture before you continue.
- Meet the stakeholder to obtain the relevant business source links and context; the facilitator supplies the interview link with the assignment. Read those online sources through the intended access route.

"""Packet readiness, recorded-decision admission, and activation.

This layer consumes the Stage 3 evaluator and recorded source documents. It
never creates a human disposition or committee outcome.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import calendar
import re
from datetime import date, timedelta
from typing import Any

from .evaluation import evaluate_application, _parse_date, _row_records, _source_ref


POLICY = {
    "readiness": ["office/procedure-extract.txt § 8 — Packet readiness", "office/procedure-extract.txt § 4 — High-risk findings"],
    "decisions": ["office/procedure-extract.txt § 9 — The committee protocol", "office/authority-roster.txt — Who may record what; Individual authority"],
    "activation": ["office/procedure-extract.txt § 10 — Activation and the appointment cycle", "office/procedure-extract.txt § 11 — Re-entry"],
}

LIMITATIONS = [
    "Stage 3 evidence limitations remain: reference delivery channel is absent from exports; accreditation status is not supplied; acceptable verifiers for teaching and military history are undefined.",
    "This implementation does not determine intake completeness, clinical competency, whether a finding is disqualifying, whether a gap explanation is satisfactory, or whether appointment should be recommended or granted.",
    "Condition completion is recognized only when a recorded source explicitly names the condition; no completion is inferred from unrelated evidence.",
    "Conditional-approval condition extraction recognizes explicit '... due YYYY-MM-DD' phrases in the recorded reason. Other condition wording is retained in decision details but cannot be converted to the schema's condition-and-date pair without an explicit structured source field.",
]

_ROLES = {
    "Chair, Governing Body": ("Ms. Corinne Batiste", date(2025, 1, 1), date(2027, 12, 31)),
    "Vice-Chair, Governing Body": ("Mr. Desmond Ihejirika", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)),
    "Chair, Executive Committee of the Medical Staff": ("Dr. Peter Vandermolen, MD", date(2026, 1, 1), date(2027, 12, 31)),
    "Chair, Credentials Committee": ("Dr. Anneke Thorvald, MD", date(2025, 7, 1), date(2027, 6, 30)),
}
_BODY_OUTCOMES = {
    "Credentials Committee": {"recommended", "not recommended", "deferred-pending-information"},
    "Executive Committee of the Medical Staff": {"recommended", "not recommended", "deferred-pending-information"},
    "Governing Body": {"approved", "approved-with-conditions", "deferred-pending-information", "denied"},
}
_NONBLOCKING_OBSERVATIONS = {
    # These describe evidence already established or a certification finding
    # limited to an unsupported subset. The procedure permits such a finding
    # to travel with a presentable packet; it is not an open verification hold.
    "gap_explained",
    "privilege_support_map",
    "two_qualifying_current_references",
    "unsupported_requested_privilege",
}


def _fields(markdown: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    return {k.strip().casefold(): v.strip() for k, v in re.findall(r"^\*\*([^*]+):\*\*[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", markdown, re.M)}


def _document_ref(batch: dict[str, Any], doc: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {"batch_id": batch.get("batch_id"), "document_path": doc.get("path"), "sha256": doc.get("sha256")}


def _app_revision_exists(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, revision: str, on: date) -> bool:
    # A later closed export can carry an application/revision that was already
    # on file on the decision date. Use its source received_date, not the date
    # the batch was published.
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        for record in batch.get("records", []):
            values = record.get("values", {})
            received = _parse_date(values.get("received_date"))
            if (record.get("filename") == "applications.csv"
                    and str(values.get("application_id")) == app_id
                    and str(values.get("revision")) == revision
                    and received is not None and received <= on):
                return True
    return False


def _historical_evidence_view(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Expose later-exported rows to date-aware evaluators for historical checks.

    The evaluator still applies each source's event dates and document dates;
    lowering only the enclosing batch cutoff avoids confusing publication date
    with when a row or document took effect.
    """
    view = dict(ledger)
    view["batches"] = []
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        copy = dict(batch)
        if (_parse_date(copy.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            copy["export_date"] = as_of.isoformat()
        view["batches"].append(copy)
    return view


def _predecision_readiness(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, revision: str, decision_date: date) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Apply the ordinary before-decision window plus the WA lookup exception."""
    prior_date = decision_date - timedelta(days=1)
    prior = assess_packet_readiness(_historical_evidence_view(ledger, prior_date), app_id, revision, prior_date.isoformat())
    day_rows = _historical_evidence_view(ledger, decision_date)
    same_day_wa_lookup = any(
        record.get("filename") == "licence-lookup-wa.csv"
        and _parse_date(record.get("values", {}).get("lookup_date")) == decision_date
        and str(record.get("values", {}).get("lastname", "")).casefold()
        for batch in day_rows.get("batches", []) for record in batch.get("records", [])
    )
    if not same_day_wa_lookup:
        return prior
    on_day = assess_packet_readiness(day_rows, app_id, revision, decision_date.isoformat())
    # Only the licensure component may use decision-day evidence. All other
    # elements remain fixed to the end of the preceding day.
    prior["blockers"] = [b for b in prior.get("blockers", []) if b.get("element") != "licensure"] + [
        b for b in on_day.get("blockers", []) if b.get("element") == "licensure"
    ]
    prior["cleared_holds"] = [h for h in prior.get("cleared_holds", []) if h.get("element") != "licensure"] + [
        h for h in on_day.get("cleared_holds", []) if h.get("element") == "licensure"
    ]
    prior["elements"]["licensure"] = on_day.get("elements", {}).get("licensure", prior["elements"].get("licensure"))
    prior["presentable"] = not prior["blockers"]
    return prior


def _dispositions(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, revision: str, as_of: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    found = []
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            continue
        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
            if "/dispositions/" not in f"/{path}" or not content:
                continue
            f = _fields(content)
            aid = f.get("application", "")
            rev = f.get("revision", revision)
            actor = f.get("recorded by", "")
            if aid == app_id and str(rev) == str(revision) and actor.startswith("Dr. Marguerite Oyelaran") and "Clinical Director" in actor:
                date_match = _parse_date(f.get("date"))
                if date_match and date_match <= as_of:
                    found.append({"fields": f, "content": content, "ref": _document_ref(batch, doc), "date": date_match})
    return found


def assess_packet_readiness(ledger: dict[str, Any], application_id: str, revision: int | str, as_of: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Assess six-element readiness as of a date, with authorized dispositions."""
    day = _parse_date(as_of)
    if day is None:
        raise ValueError("as_of must be an ISO calendar date")
    ev = evaluate_application(ledger, application_id, revision, as_of)
    dispositions = _dispositions(ledger, application_id, str(revision), day)
    cleared: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    blockers: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    nonblocking_findings: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for name, detail in ev["element_details"].items():
        state = detail["state"]
        obs = detail.get("observations", [])
        for finding in obs:
            code = finding.get("code", "")
            if code in _NONBLOCKING_OBSERVATIONS:
                nonblocking_findings.append({"element": name, **finding, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
                continue
            if code in {"licensure_finding", "gap_disposition_pending", "high_risk_finding"}:
                matching = [d for d in dispositions if
                            (code != "gap_disposition_pending" or "gap" in d["content"].casefold()) and
                            (code != "licensure_finding" or "licens" in d["content"].casefold())]
                if matching:
                    cleared.append({"element": name, "finding_code": code, "disposition": matching[-1]["ref"], "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
                    continue
                blockers.append({"element": name, "code": code, "message": finding.get("message", "Required disposition is missing."), "evidence": finding.get("evidence", detail.get("evidence", [])), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
            elif state != "resolved":
                blockers.append({"element": name, "code": code or state, "message": finding.get("message", f"Element state is {state}."), "evidence": finding.get("evidence", detail.get("evidence", [])), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
        # No observations for a non-resolved state still constitutes blocking work.
        if state != "resolved" and not obs:
            blockers.append({"element": name, "code": state, "message": f"Element state is {state}.", "evidence": detail.get("evidence", []), "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
    # High-risk disclosure evidence is outside the six element states.
    for batch, record in _row_records(ledger, day):
        v = record.get("values", {})
        if record.get("filename") == "application-disclosures.csv" and v.get("application_id") == application_id and str(v.get("revision")) == str(revision) and str(v.get("answer", "")).casefold() == "yes":
            refs = [_source_ref(batch, record)]
            matching = [d for d in dispositions if "high-risk" in d["content"].casefold()]
            if not matching:
                blockers.append({"element": "high-risk", "code": "high_risk_disposition_pending", "message": "High-risk disclosure awaits a Clinical Director disposition.", "evidence": refs, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
            else:
                cleared.append({"element": "high-risk", "finding_code": "high_risk_finding", "disposition": matching[-1]["ref"], "evidence": refs, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"]})
    return {"application_id": application_id, "revision": int(revision), "as_of": as_of,
            "presentable": not blockers, "elements": ev["elements"], "blockers": blockers,
            "cleared_holds": cleared, "nonblocking_findings": nonblocking_findings,
            "evaluation": ev, "rule_refs": POLICY["readiness"],
            "limitations": LIMITATIONS}


def _parse_decisions(ledger: dict[str, Any], as_of: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    out = []
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            continue
        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
            if "/decisions/" not in f"/{path}" or not content:
                continue
            f = _fields(content)
            if not f.get("decision id"):
                continue
            f["__ref"] = _document_ref(batch, doc)
            f["__content"] = content
            out.append(f)
    return out


def _decision_conditions(d: dict[str, Any]) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Read explicitly listed condition/due pairs from a decision record."""
    content = d.get("__content", "")
    section = re.search(r"^\*\*Conditions:\*\*[ \t]*\r?\n(.*?)(?=^##\s|\Z)", content, re.M | re.S)
    lines = section.group(1).splitlines() if section else []
    result = []
    for line in lines:
        item = re.match(r"\s*[-*]\s+(.+?)\s+[—–-]\s+due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$", line, re.I)
        if item and _parse_date(item.group(2)):
            result.append({"condition": item.group(1).strip(), "due": item.group(2)})
    # Older records may place a single explicit due-dated condition in Reason.
    if not result:
        for item in (d.get("reason") or "").split(";"):
            match = re.match(r"\s*(.*?)\s+due\s+(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s*$", item, re.I)
            if match and _parse_date(match.group(2)):
                result.append({"condition": match.group(1).strip(), "due": match.group(2)})
    return result


def _terminal_status(ledger: dict[str, Any], app_id: str, as_of: date) -> tuple[str | None, dict[str, Any] | None]:
    """Find explicit applicant withdrawal or roster-authorized discontinuance."""
    for batch in ledger.get("batches", []):
        if (_parse_date(batch.get("export_date")) or date.max) > as_of:
            continue
        for doc in batch.get("documents", []):
            path, content = doc.get("path", ""), doc.get("content", "")
            if not content:
                continue
            fields = _fields(content)
            if fields.get("application") != app_id:
                continue
            if "/letters/" in f"/{path}" and re.search(r"\bI am withdrawing my application\b", content, re.I):
                when = _parse_date(fields.get("date"))
                if when and when <= as_of:
                    return "withdrawn", _document_ref(batch, doc)
    for disposition in _dispositions(ledger, app_id, "1", as_of):
        content = disposition["content"]
        if re.search(r"\bDiscontinue the application\b", content, re.I) and not re.search(r"\bDo not discontinue the application\b", content, re.I):
            return "discontinued", disposition["ref"]
    return None, None


def _cycle_end(effective: date) -> date:
    year = effective.year + 1
    anniversary = effective.replace(year=year, day=min(effective.day, calendar.monthrange(year, effective.month)[1]))
    return anniversary - timedelta(days=1)


def _admit_decision(ledger: dict[str, Any], d: dict[str, Any], target_app: str, target_rev: str, readiness_cache: dict[tuple[str, str, str], dict[str, Any]]) -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    decision_date = _parse_date(d.get("decision date"))

command: sed -n '10,32p' office/export-notes.txt && sed -n '110,135p' office/procedure-extract.txt && sed -n '45,95p' office/privilege-criteria.txt
item.stdout:
So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.
The files
Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
File
	One row is
	applications.csv
	an application revision I received in the window
	application-disclosures.csv
	one professional practice question and the applicant's answer
	declared-history.csv
	one history entry the applicant declared
	declared-credentials.csv
	one licence or certification as the applicant described it
	privilege-requests.csv
	one privilege group requested
	licence-lookup-wa.csv
	one Washington credential record from the state board's lookup
	licence-lookup-other-states.csv
	one out-of-state credential record
	certification-replies.csv
	one certifying board's reply
	verification-replies.csv
	one reply about education and training, or about an affiliation or employer
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
	Completion of an accredited obstetrics and gynecology residency, 48 months
	Obstetric or gynaecological practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-PED
	Pediatrics — outpatient and inpatient care of patients under 18
	American Board of Pediatrics (ABP), Pediatrics; American Osteopathic Board of Pediatrics (AOBP), Pediatrics
	Completion of an accredited pediatrics residency, 36 months
	Patient care in the specialty within the last 24 months
	PRIV-ANES
	Anesthesiology — general and regional anaesthesia, peri-operative care
	American Board of Anesthesiology (ABA), Anesthesiology; American Osteopathic Board of Anesthesiology (AOBA)
	Completion of an accredited anesthesiology residency, 48 months
	Anaesthetic practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-RAD
	Diagnostic Radiology — interpretation of diagnostic imaging
	American Board of Radiology (ABR), Diagnostic Radiology; American Osteopathic Board of Radiology (AOBR), Diagnostic Radiology
	Completion of an accredited diagnostic radiology residency, 48 months
	Interpretive practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-PSY
	Psychiatry — inpatient and outpatient psychiatric care of adults
	American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), Psychiatry; American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry (AOBNP), Psychiatry
	Completion of an accredited psychiatry residency, 48 months
	Psychiatric practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-ORTHO
	Orthopaedic Surgery — elective and trauma orthopaedic procedures
	American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery (ABOS), Orthopaedic Surgery; American Osteopathic Board of Orthopedic Surgery (AOBOS), Orthopedic Surgery
	Completion of an accredited orthopaedic surgery residency, 60 months
	Operative practice within the last 24 months
	The boards named above are real certifying bodies. Nothing in these materials is a statement about any practitioner they have actually certified.
How the office applies the table
1. A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
2. A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.

So: do not diff a later batch against an earlier one looking for edits. There are none. What a later batch contains is new rows, new documents and new observations.
The files
Thirteen comma-separated exports, and three folders of documents.
File
	One row is
	applications.csv
	an application revision I received in the window
	application-disclosures.csv
	one professional practice question and the applicant's answer
	declared-history.csv
	one history entry the applicant declared
	declared-credentials.csv
	one licence or certification as the applicant described it
	privilege-requests.csv
	one privilege group requested
	licence-lookup-wa.csv
	one Washington credential record from the state board's lookup
	licence-lookup-other-states.csv
	one out-of-state credential record
	certification-replies.csv
	one certifying board's reply
	verification-replies.csv
	one reply about education and training, or about an affiliation or employer
"All peer references are from a professional authority who has worked directly with the applicant within the past two years and can authoritatively speak to the applicant's character, clinical experience, and competency."
"the IHS definition of a peer includes a practitioner in the same clinical discipline."
"A peer must not be a relative, spouse, or partner."
Three disqualifiers, each independent: not worked together directly inside two years; not in the same clinical discipline; a relative, spouse or partner. A referee who fails any one of them does not count, and we find out only when the reply arrives and states the relationship.
Larkhollow rule — how each of the three is measured. The manual gives the conditions and not the arithmetic, so ours is:
* Worked together within two years is measured against the date the referee signs, because that is the day the referee attests to it. A referee whose last date working directly with the applicant is earlier than two years before their own signature date does not qualify. A blank last date means they still work together and the condition holds.
* Same clinical discipline is the discipline the referee states on the returned form against the discipline the applicant declared on the application. Both come from a fixed list.
* Relative, spouse or partner is the box the referee ticks on the returned form, read with whatever they wrote beside it.
Currency, from Section 8:
"Peer references are considered current if the reference's signature is within two years of the file presentation to the GB."
The signature date, not the date we received it. A reference can go stale while the file waits.
Larkhollow rule — when currency is measured. A reference is current when the presentation date is on or before the second anniversary of the signature date. For a file the Governing Body has decided, the presentation date is the decision date. For a file not yet decided, we measure currency against today, so that a reference about to go stale is visible before the committee meets rather than afterwards.
Larkhollow rule — the reference window. The manual states how many times to ask and does not state how long to wait. Ours: 21 calendar days per request, up to three requests. Request one goes out, request two 21 days later, request three 21 days after that. From day 64 after the first request the reference is overdue: we tell the applicant and ask for an additional referee. The original request stays open and stays outstanding; it is never closed as satisfied and never counted.
Larkhollow rule — the floor is two. Two qualifying, current references, both eligible on all three disqualifiers, both signed inside two years of the presentation date. An ineligible referee does not count towards the two even though the reply is in the file.
Larkhollow rule — an open request does not hold a met element. Once two qualifying, current references are on file, the peer-reference element is resolved. A request that is still open is carried on the action list until the file is presented and is then closed as no longer needed; it is never counted, and it does not hold the element or the file.
Check 5 — Board certification and the privileges requested
The manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 5:
"At the initial appointment, all active and inactive board certifications are verified."
"Verified through the certifying board."
All of them — a lapsed certificate is verified too, because what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts and the file needs both.
On whether a certification supports a privilege, the manual gives the duty to clinical leadership:
"MSPs will check the facility's privilege criteria and conditions of employment (for IHS employees, review the position description, and for contractors, review the contract) to determine if the LP meets the board-certified/board-eligible requirements."
"The facility's clinical leadership is responsible for ensuring that the LP's board-certified or board eligibility aligns with the requested privileges."
and Section 9 says what criteria must address:
"At a minimum, privilege criteria should address the required education level, formal training requirements, and current experience."
Larkhollow rule — the criteria are published and versioned. privilege-criteria.md maps each privilege group to the certifying boards that support it and to a minimum training requirement, under a version string. Every decision record cites the criteria version it was decided under. The office applies the map; the office does not write it and does not extend it.
	Completion of an accredited obstetrics and gynecology residency, 48 months
	Obstetric or gynaecological practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-PED
	Pediatrics — outpatient and inpatient care of patients under 18
	American Board of Pediatrics (ABP), Pediatrics; American Osteopathic Board of Pediatrics (AOBP), Pediatrics
	Completion of an accredited pediatrics residency, 36 months
	Patient care in the specialty within the last 24 months
	PRIV-ANES
	Anesthesiology — general and regional anaesthesia, peri-operative care
	American Board of Anesthesiology (ABA), Anesthesiology; American Osteopathic Board of Anesthesiology (AOBA)
	Completion of an accredited anesthesiology residency, 48 months
	Anaesthetic practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-RAD
	Diagnostic Radiology — interpretation of diagnostic imaging
	American Board of Radiology (ABR), Diagnostic Radiology; American Osteopathic Board of Radiology (AOBR), Diagnostic Radiology
	Completion of an accredited diagnostic radiology residency, 48 months
	Interpretive practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-PSY
	Psychiatry — inpatient and outpatient psychiatric care of adults
	American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN), Psychiatry; American Osteopathic Board of Neurology and Psychiatry (AOBNP), Psychiatry
	Completion of an accredited psychiatry residency, 48 months
	Psychiatric practice within the last 24 months
	PRIV-ORTHO
	Orthopaedic Surgery — elective and trauma orthopaedic procedures
	American Board of Orthopaedic Surgery (ABOS), Orthopaedic Surgery; American Osteopathic Board of Orthopedic Surgery (AOBOS), Orthopedic Surgery
	Completion of an accredited orthopaedic surgery residency, 60 months
	Operative practice within the last 24 months
	The boards named above are real certifying bodies. Nothing in these materials is a statement about any practitioner they have actually certified.
How the office applies the table
1. A requested group is supported when the applicant holds a verified certification from one of the boards named in that group's row, in the specialty named, with certification_status Active on the decision date, and the verified training meets the minimum training requirement.
2. A requested group is unsupported when neither condition holds. The finding names that group. Other requested groups are unaffected.
3. An inactive or expired certification does not support a privilege group. It is still verified and still recorded — what the applicant is certified in and what the applicant was once certified in are different facts — but it supports nothing.
4. Board eligible is accepted in place of an active certification for PRIV-FM, PRIV-IM, PRIV-HOSP and PRIV-PED only, and only when the issuing board confirms in writing that the applicant is a candidate in good standing and states the date the eligibility ends, and that date is in the future on the decision date. Board eligible is not accepted for PRIV-CARD, PRIV-EM, PRIV-GS, PRIV-OBG, PRIV-ANES, PRIV-RAD, PRIV-PSY or PRIV-ORTHO.
5. PRIV-CARD requires both: the cardiovascular disease fellowship and the internal medicine residency that precedes it. A cardiology certification without the residency, or the residency without the fellowship, does not support it.
6. When nothing the applicant holds supports any requested group, this is a threshold eligibility question. The office raises it to the Clinical Director, who decides whether the application is discontinued. The office does not discontinue an application. The office raises it on what has been verified at the export date: while nothing yet verified supports any requested group, the question stands with the Clinical Director, and it is withdrawn without a disposition when a later verification supports the request.
7. The current-experience column is not the office's to apply. Current competency is determined by clinical leadership, not the office (the manual, Section 6, Subsection 4, element 8), and it is one of the elements this procedure does not handle. Whether a group is supported is decided by rules 1 to 6 alone; the current-experience requirement travels with the packet for the committee and never makes a group unsupported.
Whether a supported request should be granted is not settled here. That is the Executive Committee of the Medical Staff's recommendation and the Governing Body's decision.

def _license_element(
    element: _Element, rows: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]], app: dict[str, Any],
    application_id: str, revision: str, as_of: date,
    docs: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]],
) -> None:
    identity = tuple(str(app.get(field) or "") for field in ("last_name", "first_name", "middle_name", "birth_year"))
    declared = [
        (batch, record) for batch, record in rows
        if record.get("filename") == "declared-credentials.csv"
        and record.get("values", {}).get("application_id") == application_id
        and record.get("values", {}).get("revision") == revision
        and str(record.get("values", {}).get("credential_class") or "").casefold() in {"licence", "license"}
    ]
    for batch, record in declared:
        element.cite(batch, record)
    wa_rows = [
        (batch, record) for batch, record in rows
        if record.get("filename") == "licence-lookup-wa.csv"
        and tuple(str(record.get("values", {}).get(field) or "") for field in ("lastname", "firstname", "middlename", "birthyear")) == identity
    ]
    other_rows = [
        (batch, record) for batch, record in rows
        if record.get("filename") == "licence-lookup-other-states.csv"
    ]
    matched: dict[str, list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]] = {}
    for item in wa_rows:
        number = item[1]["values"].get("credentialnumber")
        if number:
            matched.setdefault(str(number), []).append(item)
    for declared_batch, declared_record in declared:
        dv = declared_record["values"]
        number = str(dv.get("number_declared") or "")
        jurisdiction = str(dv.get("jurisdiction_or_board") or "").upper()
        candidates = matched.get(number, []) if jurisdiction == "WA" else []
        if jurisdiction != "WA":
            candidates = [
                (b, r) for b, r in other_rows
                if str(r.get("values", {}).get("licence_number") or "") == number
                and str(r.get("values", {}).get("board_state") or "").upper() == jurisdiction
            ]
        if not candidates:
            element.note("licence_verification_outstanding", f"No board lookup row is linked to declared licence {number!r} ({jurisdiction}).", [_source_ref(declared_batch, declared_record)])
            continue
        for lookup_batch, lookup_record in candidates:
            lv = lookup_record["values"]
            element.cite(lookup_batch, lookup_record)
            if jurisdiction != "WA":
                verified_by = str(lv.get("verified_by") or "").casefold()
                accepted = ("board" in verified_by and "online verification" in verified_by) or "physician data center" in verified_by
                if not accepted:
                    element.note("inadmissible_license_source", f"Out-of-state licence source {lv.get('verified_by')!r} is not established as a listed board/FSMB source.", [_source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record)])
                    continue
            lookup_date = _parse_date(lv.get("lookup_date"))
            if lookup_date is None or lookup_date > as_of:
                element.note("invalid_license_lookup_date", f"Licence lookup date {lv.get('lookup_date')!r} is missing, invalid, or after the export date.", [_source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record)])
                continue
            state = str(lv.get("status") or lv.get("license_status") or "").casefold()
            action = str(lv.get("actiontaken") or lv.get("disciplinary_action") or "").casefold()
            action_detail_classified = False
            if action not in {"", "no", "none", "none reported", "false"}:
                if action not in {"yes", "pending", "true"} and any(term in action for term in ("probation", "supervision", "monitoring agreement", "practice limitation", "suspend", "stipulated condition", "surrender", "restriction")):
                    element.note("licensure_finding", f"Board record states an adverse licence condition for {number!r}; preserve and route to the Clinical Director.", [_source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record)])
            expiration = _parse_date(lv.get("expirationdate") or lv.get("expiry_date"))
            if jurisdiction == "WA" and (state != "active" or expiration is None or expiration < as_of):
                element.note("washington_license_not_current", f"Washington lookup does not show licence {number!r} as active and unexpired on {as_of.isoformat()}.", [_source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record)])
            if jurisdiction == "WA" and any(term in action for term in ("yes", "pending", "stipulated", "probation", "supervision", "restriction")):
                for doc_batch, index_record, document in docs:
                    content = document.get("content", "")
                    if number in content:
                        detail = content.casefold()
                        fields = {k.strip().casefold(): v.strip() for k, v in re.findall(r"^\*\*([^*]+):\*\*[ \t]*(.*?)[ \t]*$", content, re.M)}
                        source_name = fields.get("from", "").casefold()
                        if not any(term in source_name for term in ("washington state department of health", "washington medical commission", "state licensing board")):
                            continue
                        element.cite(doc_batch, index_record, document.get("path"))
                        restrictive = any(term in detail for term in (
                            "stipulated agreement", "under supervision", "monitoring programme", "monitoring program",
                            "practice limitation", "on probation", "suspended", "surrendered", "practice restriction",
                        ))
                        negated = any(phrase in detail for phrase in (
                            "no practice restriction", "no restriction is in force", "not restricted", "no monitoring agreement",
                        ))
                        if restrictive and not negated:
                            action_detail_classified = True
                            element.note("licensure_finding", f"Indexed board document describes a restriction for licence {number!r}; preserve it without judging its significance.", [
                                _source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record), _source_ref(doc_batch, index_record, document.get("path"))
                            ])
                        elif negated:
                            action_detail_classified = True
            if action in {"yes", "pending", "true"} and not action_detail_classified:
                element.note("board_action_requires_detail", f"Board lookup indicates action ({action}); an authoritative written board detail classifying the action is not on file.", [_source_ref(lookup_batch, lookup_record)])

    declared_numbers = {str(r[1]["values"].get("number_declared") or "") for r in declared}
    for batch, record in wa_rows:
        number = str(record["values"].get("credentialnumber") or "")
        if number and number not in declared_numbers:
            element.cite(batch, record)
            declared_sources = [_source_ref(b, r) for b, r in declared]
            element.note("undeclared_washington_license", f"Washington lookup contains credential {number!r}, absent from this revision's declared licences.", [_source_ref(batch, record), *declared_sources])

    active_wa = []
    for batch, record in wa_rows:
        values = record["values"]
        expiration = _parse_date(values.get("expirationdate"))
        if str(values.get("status") or "").casefold() == "active" and expiration is not None and expiration >= as_of:
            active_wa.append((batch, record))
    if not active_wa:
        application_sources = [
            _source_ref(batch, record) for batch, record in rows
            if record.get("filename") == "applications.csv"
            and record.get("values", {}).get("application_id") == application_id
            and str(record.get("values", {}).get("revision")) == revision
        ]
        element.note("washington_practice_license_missing", "No current active Washington licence is present in the joined board lookup on the export date.", [
            *[_source_ref(batch, record) for batch, record in wa_rows], *application_sources,
        ])
        element.problems.add("finding")

def _add_months(day: date, months: int) -> date:
    month_index = day.month - 1 + months
    year = day.year + month_index // 12
    month = month_index % 12 + 1
    return date(year, month, min(day.day, calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]))


def _training_support(
    requirements: list[tuple[str, str, int]],
    history: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]],
    rows: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]],
    application_id: str,
    first_received: date,
    as_of: date,
    docs: list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]],
) -> tuple[bool, list[dict[str, Any]], bool]:
    evidence = []
    accredited_missing = False

    # Every privilege group also requires a verified MD/DO from an accredited
    # school. The export has no accreditation column, so accreditation must be
    # stated in the accepted registrar reply itself; it is never presumed.
    degree_verified = False
    degree_entries = [
        (b, r) for b, r in history
        if str(r.get("values", {}).get("entry_type") or "").casefold() == "medical-school"
    ]
    for entry_batch, entry_record in degree_entries:
        ev = entry_record["values"]
        evidence.append(_source_ref(entry_batch, entry_record))
        replies = _entry_replies(rows, application_id, str(ev.get("entry_id") or ""), "education-and-training")
        for reply_batch, reply_record in replies:
            rv = reply_record["values"]
            source_class, _ = _source_class("education-and-training", rv, docs)
            usable, _ = _reply_is_usable(rv, first_received, as_of)
            if source_class == "inadmissible" or not usable or str(rv.get("outcome") or "").casefold() != "confirmed":
                continue
            if not _parse_date(rv.get("verified_from")) or not _parse_date(rv.get("verified_to")):
                continue
            text = (str(rv.get("verified_credential") or "") + " " + str(rv.get("notes") or "")).casefold()
            if not any(term in text for term in ("doctor of medicine", "doctor of osteopathic medicine")):
                continue
            evidence.append(_source_ref(reply_batch, reply_record))
            if _has_positive_accreditation(text):
                degree_verified = True
                break
            accredited_missing = True
        if degree_verified:
            break
    if not degree_verified:
        # No medical-school response or no explicit accreditation proof is not
        # evidence of an unqualified school; it is an unresolved requirement.
        return False, evidence, True

    for entry_type, specialty, minimum_months in requirements:
        matched = False
